articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Meandered Line RFID Reader Antennas for UHF Near Field Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research looks into and analyzes in detail the design of a meandered line RFID reader antenna, which is mainly meant for near-field applications. The Ultra-High frequency (UHF) band, which spans from 840 MHz to 960 MHz, is where the antenna operates. The scope of the study involves the comparative study of design variations of the RFID reader antenna, which involves the insertion and deletion of the U-shaped section within the meandered line antenna design and the E-shaped middle section within the meandered line antenna design. The following design variations demonstrate an improvement in the overall gain and polarization pattern of the antenna. In addition to this, the antenna designs depict a lower far-field gain that prevents the incorrect reading of designated targets outside the near-field region. Circular polarization is observed when the U-shaped section is incorporated within the antenna design, which exhibited a return loss of [S11] = -13.25 dB, near-field antenna gain of - 4.73 dBi, and an operating frequency of 878.8 MHz, which covers the UHF RFID range. The proposed antennas are designed and simulated using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio software.

articleTitle: The Role of Deep Learning in Transforming Cassava Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The cultivation and output of cassava, the most important crop in the Philippines, are greatly endangered by a number of illnesses. Because cassava is essential for food security, it is crucial to identify these illnesses in their early stages before they worsen. The approaches utilised in disease identification are based on the expert knowledge of fuzzy domain products and the framers’ experience. This paper proposes an automated system for illness identification using pretrained neural network models and deep learning, with inspiration from convolutional neural network techniques. The system would deal with fuzzy input. Consequently, the suggested neural network systems automatically detected red leach and anthocyanin. In this case, a model was trained using transfer learning on the EfficientnetB3 configuration, which had 10,791,220 learnable parameters, in order to deal with fuzzy data for cassava disease diagnosis. With the suggested data model, which incorporates the same, the accuracy reached was 89.90%, surpassing the 50.46% baseline proportionate chance consideration. In spite of data imbalances, the neural network classifier still manages to identify cassava leaf disease with remarkable accuracy. Improved crop yields aren't the only thing that farmers and agricultural researchers can do with our findings. In order to avoid crop failure, our method of disease detection may automate data collecting for disease diagnosis. Our findings lead us to suggest the following studies as potential avenues for further study into plant disease detection at a larger scale.

articleTitle: Insect Classification Using Mel-CSTFT: A Fusion of Mel Spectrogram and Chroma STFT Features
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Insect audio classification has witnessed substantial advancements in recent years, facilitated by the development of CNNs and deep learning architectures, which have demonstrated improved performance. Typically used hand-crafted features, specifically MFCCs, have consistently achieved state-of-the-art results in various signal processing research works. However, there is still a lot of scope, and since CNNs and deep neural networks have great capabilities in learning essential information from image-based features, sound signals extracted as visual representations, such as in the form of mel spectrograms, are now being frequently used for classification and detection purposes. To enhance the robustness and reliability of these features, researchers have adopted various techniques, including feature fusion, denoising, data augmentation, transfer learning, and attention mechanisms, etc. Therefore, this study presents a fusion called Mel-CSTFT, comprising of two sound features - mel spectrograms and chroma STFT, and conducts a performance analysis of this combination against the individual features. Ultimately, the aim is to identify whether this combination can outperform the performance of mel spectrograms, which have demonstrated impressive performance in multiple works, and to assess its robustness and reliability across a diverse and relatively bigger dataset.

articleTitle: Priority-Based Resource Allocation in Vehicular Communication Using Q-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)

authors.preferredName: K. L. V. Sai Prakash Sakuru

abstract: Vehicular communication has the potential to revolutionize road safety, traffic efficiency, infotainment services, and autonomous driving. However, as urban traffic complexity increases, intelligent transportation solutions are essential. Priority-based resource allocation is crucial for optimizing network performance and information transmission efficiency in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). In this context, Q- learning optimizes resource allocation in vehicular communication systems, prioritizing real-time traffic conditions. The Q-learning model effectively allocates resources based on priority, continuously improving strategy over time. This study shows the significant potential of the Q-Learning model for optimizing priority-based resource allocation in vehicular communication, enhancing road safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: Real Time Video Processing Using Polar Fire FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This effort aims to create a hardware resource-efficient real-time video processing system employing Polar Fire FPGA technology. This paper presents the interface between two IMX 334 camera modules and a Polar-Fire FPGA and displays the video to the 1920 x 1080 monitor output via HDMI 1.4 TX port in picture in picture mode. The IMX 334 camera module supports CSI2 serial data output (4 lane/8lane, RAW10/RAW12 output) at 60 frames per second at full HD and at 30 fps at 4k resolution. The solution comes with an easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) for controlling image and video settings, along with picture-in-picture mode features.

articleTitle: Smart Solutions for Utilizing Advanced Machine Learning for Robust Credit Card Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research primarily aims to shed light on the serious issue of credit card fraud, which has become much worse with the advent of internet shopping and, more specifically, the present COVID-19 epidemic. Developing a machine learning system capable of distinguishing between legitimate and fraudulent credit card transactions is the primary objective of this project, which aims to decrease an annual loss of ∃24 billion. Using data such as transformed numerical characteristics after PCA analyses, transaction time and amount, and Logistic Regression, Decision Tree Classifier, and K-Nearest Neighbours approaches are employed in the research study. The accuracy rates of these algorithms are demonstrated by the cross-validation score, ROC AUC score, and F1 score within the context of fraud detection. Improving the models’ accuracy and resilience is as simple as using statistical tests like ANOVA when selecting features. To improve the detection of fraudulent behaviour and to accurately compare the results of various algorithms, balanced datasets are essential, as this shows. There was a 91% F1 score, 92.35% ROC AUC, and 98.01% crossvalidation accuracy rate for fraud detection in the logistic regression model. Alternatively, a decision tree classifier's fraud detection cross-validation score was 96.67%, ROC AUC was 91.36%, and F1 was 90%. When it came to detecting fraud, K-Nearest Neighbours performed exceptionally well with scores of 97.63% for ROC AUC, 99.34% for cross-validation, and 97% for F1.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in Advanced Analog Building Blocks Using Ensemble Stacking Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Detecting faults in large integrated electronic building blocks is challenging due to the intricate operating mechanisms. As electronics evolve, diagnosing faults in complex analog systems becomes harder. Hence, it is crucial to promptly and precisely detect problems in analogue circuits. This study introduces a new method, ensemble stacking, to improve fault diagnosis accuracy in advanced analog block i.e., cascode and differential amplifier stages. We also showed that CatBoost outperforms other classifiers such as decision trees, logistic regression, and SVM with 96% accuracy on a cascode amplifier and 97% accuracy on a differential amplifier circuit. However, ensemble stacking achieves 100% accuracy for the first test circuit and 99.95% for the second, enhancing precision and reliability in fault diagnosis for analog circuits.

articleTitle: Vanadium Dioxide (VO2) Based Wideband Tunable Terahertz Metamaterial Polarization-Insensitive Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this presented research paper, the proposed design of a wideband tunable terahertz (THz) absorber using the phase-changing material VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The absorber has a wide bandwidth of 76.2% from 3.70 to 8.25 THz with an absorption level of more than 95%. For oblique incidents, the THz wave has an absorption level of more than 65% up to 60° incident angles. Due to the presence of the symmetry of the structure, it exhibits polarization-insensitive characteristics for both TE and TM THz-wave. Moreover, by changing the phase of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> from insulator to conductor 200 to 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> S/m with temperature, the absorption level can be varied from 2% to 98% under the wideband. The proposed absorber could be useful in absorber devices for terahertz technology in fields such as energy harvesting, imaging and security.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Schmitt Trigger Designs in 90nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of various CMOS Schmitt triggers utilized in the VLSI industry for mitigating noise effects. This paper conduct a comparative assessment of different CMOS Schmitt trigger designs, delving into their respective architectures and operational principles. The study includes a comprehensive discussion of the design intricacies of each Schmitt trigger architecture. Furthermore, we present a comparative evaluation of these architectures based on key parameters such as hysteresis width, power consumption, delay, and noise. Our findings reveal that no single architecture satisfies all specification requirements. Consequently, we perform a comparative study focusing on widely adopted architectures in GPIO buffers. This enables designers to make informed decisions regarding the most suitable design architecture based on specific project requirements. All simulations were conducted using CADENCE Virtuoso in the Spectre simulator, employing 90nm CMOS Technology.

articleTitle: Efficient Relay Selection in NOMA-Based Cooperative Networks: A Supervised Learning Approach With Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this research, we examine how machine learning is used to cooperative communication networks' relay selection, emphasizing transmission under non-orthogonal multiple access. We introduce a novel relay selection algorithm based on Random Forest and compare its performance with SVM method previously discussed in this context and enhanced two- stage max-min selection rule. According to the study results, the Random Forest algorithm shows improved outage probability and system throughput even when the signal regime is more difficult. The superiority of the presented algorithm lies in its ability to combine NOMA and OMA transmission sources in an intelligent way, as well as ensure adaptability even in more complex situations due to high-dimensional classification. This work provides readers with valuable experience in applying machine learning methods to improve communication systems.

articleTitle: Generic Parametrized Cell Design Methodology for Analog and Mixedsignal Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The advancement of analog and mixed-signal circuit design demands methodologies that combine efficiency with adaptability. This paper presents a basic Parametrized Cell (PCell) Design Methodology, which employs the SKILL language for the creation of highly adaptable primitive cells. Our methodology facilitates swift parametric adjustments to meet diverse design specifications, ensuring design consistency and minimizing manual errors. To design a basic pcell we incorporate SKILL code blocks such as a constructor block for initial parameter setup, a cdf block for defining interactive parameter interfaces, a callback block for parameter changes responses, and a pcellMaster block for the main cell generation logic. The paper explores the advantages of PCell development, such as enhanced design reusability and the streamlining of design automation. It also addresses the challenges faced, including the learning curve associated with the SKILL language and the complexity of encapsulating various design constraints within a parametric model.[1] Despite these challenges, the methodology offers substantial reductions in design time and improvements in circuit robustness. Case studies are presented to illustrate the methodology's efficacy in optimizing the design process, highlighting its significant contributions to the field of integrated circuit design.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characterization of Proposed SRAM Cell at 16nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The paper offers an in-depth analysis and design assessment of SRAM cells, focusing on important performance indicators. The article starts off with a summary of memory types, emphasizing the importance of SRAM in a variety of applications. The paper investigates the merits and demerits of multiple SRAM cell topologies for 16nm technology. In order to assess the suggested 9T cell against other SRAM designs that are currently in use, its power delay product, power consumption, and overall delay have all been examined. The results of the simulation show that although the 9T SRAM cell's delay is noticeably less, it consumes more power than other alternative technologies. In a comparison analysis, the performance of the proposed 9T SRAM cell is compared with that of 6T, 7T, and 10T SRAM cells at 16nm technology.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of 12-nm Gate-all-Around Vertically Stacked Nanosheet Field Effect Transistor for High-k Gate-oxide Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: As the dimensions of 2D FETs decrease, issues such as short-channel effects emerge, prompting the search for improved device designs. 3D structures like FinFETs offer enhanced gate controllability and better electrical characteristics. Despite this, short channel effects remain a concern for FinFETs with channel lengths below 22 nm. This has led to the adoption of GAAFETs (gate-all-around FETs), which provide gate coverage from all directions. GAAFETs represent the latest advancement in 3D device technology and are increasingly utilized in chip manufacturing processes. In the work below, we studied the electrical properties of a 12-nm vertically stacked nanosheet gate-all-around field effect transistor (VNSFET) by varying gate-oxide material and replacing gate-oxide material with high- k dielectric materials (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, HfSiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Temperature variations for devices are also considered along gate oxide dielectric variations The obtained results showed that ON current increases and OFF current decreases with the increase in dielectric constant. We compared our simulation results with predicted data from the International Roadmap for Devices and Systems [2]. Additionally, it was observed that TiO2 is superior to other gate oxides.

articleTitle: Design of Triangular Shaped Graphene Patch Antenna for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this paper a triangular shaped slotted graphene patch antenna over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> substrate is designed for terahertz applications. The radiating patch is fed with CPW feedline. The overall size of antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$48\times 52\times 3\mu \mathrm{m}^{3}$</tex>. Return loss and radiation patterns are obtained and analyzed using HFSS 11.1 tool. The designed antenna resonates in terahertz regime from 3.2 - 30 THz, which makes it suitable for applications such as biomedical imaging, terahertz imaging and wireless communication.

articleTitle: Spectrally Efficient Approach of Wavelength Conversion Employing Non-Linearity and Polarized Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Wavelength converters is a crucial element in optical communication networks. It plays a climacteric role in enhancing signal quality, enabling seamless data transmission, allowing faster transmission, and providing greater bandwidth. These Wavelength converters can be mileage by using fiber nonlinearities, Semiconductor Optical Amplifier (SOA) nonlinearities, Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifier (EDFA) nonlinearities, etc. Polarization multiplexing has emerged as a promising approach to wavelength conversion, leveraging the unique characteristics of polarized light to manipulate signals effectively. In this study, a design and performance evaluation of a wavelength converter employing polarization multiplexing was proposed. The implementation and simulation were carried out using the OptiSystem software. The proposed wavelength converter capitalizes on the unique properties of polarization multiplexing for achieving efficient and tunable optical wavelength conversion. The design process encompasses the meticulous selection of optical components within the OptiSystem environment, such as polarization-sensitive elements, modulators, and detectors. Performance evaluation metrics, including conversion efficiency, signal quality, bit error rate, and quality factor of the signal, were comprehensively analyzed through extensive simulations in the OptiSystem software.

articleTitle: Design of Combined Temperature and Humidity Chipless RFID Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The rapid advancements, in technology have resulted in the adoption of RFID for purposes like managing inventory optimizing supply chains tracking assets and controlling access. One promising area where RFID technology shines is in sensing applications. With its ability to capture real time data and monitor effectively, RFID technology is especially well suited for sensing. The chipless RFID sensor seeks to address the limitations of traditional sensors by leveraging the real time data capture and monitoring capabilities provided by RFID technology. By incorporating temperature and humidity sensing into chipless RFID tags the functionality and adaptability of these sensors are significantly improved. This initiative focuses on developing a chipless RFID sensor that can measure both temperature and humidity using a tag. Through the use of materials that're sensitive to both parameters and can be printed in environments our goal is to create an affordable versatile and precise sensor that will have broad applications across industries such, as agriculture, healthcare and manufacturing.

articleTitle: Stage Prediction of Liver Cirrhosis Disease using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Liver cirrhosis is a critical blood-borne disease that often remains asymptomatic in its early stages, complicating early diagnosis and treatment. As the disease progresses, diagnosing and managing it becomes increasingly challenging. This project aims to develop an artificial intelligence system utilizing machine learning algorithms to aid healthcare professionals in the early detection of liver cirrhosis. Specifically, the goal is to create a predictive system that can determine the stages of liver cirrhosis using machine learning techniques. The project will involve a comparative analysis of several established supervised learning models and ensemble learning techniques, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, and Gradient Boosting Classifier. These models will be evaluated for their accuracy and precision. The dataset for this project consists of 418 records and 20 attributes. Key steps in the project include conducting exploratory data analysis, establishing baseline models, and evaluating them using hold-out validation and k-fold cross-validation. Feature engineering techniques will also be employed to enhance model accuracy. The most effective model will be selected and deployed as the final predictive system, which will be accessible through a web application developed with the Streamlit library.

articleTitle: Ground Station based Point Ahead Angle Derivation & Variability for Spacecraft in Highly Elliptical Orbits
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study focuses on the mathematical derivation and variations of the Point Ahead Angle (PAA) from ground stations for spacecraft operating in highly elliptical orbits (HEO's), that are in most of the cases geostationary transfer orbits (GTO's). The Point Ahead Angle is a critical parameter for maintaining communication links between ground stations and spacecraft, particularly in orbits with significant eccentricity. Through detailed mathematical analysis, this research derives the complex formulas required to compute the Point Ahead Angle for spacecraft traversing highly elliptical orbits. By conducting comprehensive simulations, we analyse the dependencies of the Point Ahead Angle on orbital eccentricity, station locations, and communication techniques especially free space optical communication. This paper presents precise formulas for calculating the Point Ahead Angle for HEO's and evaluates its variability under different orbital and spacecraft's velocity conditions. By offering a thorough understanding of Point Ahead Angle derivation and its variability, this research contributes to the enhancement of communication systems for spacecraft in highly elliptical GTO's, facilitating efficient data transmission and mission success.

articleTitle: Novel Ensemble Sentiment Classification through Speech Processing and Stacking Generalization
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for speech sentiment analysis, by employing a stacking classifier. The proposed system directly transcribes audio and extracts essential features for sentiment analysis. The stacking classifier, which combines multiple classifiers, enhances predictive performance. Intermediate models include K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Random Forest, SVM, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Logistic Regression. OpenAI Whisper transformer is used for audio-to-text conversion. The methodology encompasses audio data preprocessing, text conversion, natural language processing, and model training. The model is evaluated on accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score. We examine the effectiveness of various classifiers and feature sets in sentiment analysis of speech data through empirical investigation. The experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to accurately classify sentiment and provide valuable insights into sentiment analysis methods, tailored for spoken language.

articleTitle: A Single Band Microstrip Modified Rectangular Antenna Having Rectangular and Square Slot Cuts in Patch and Ground for 39GHz Application Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: A new innovative microstrip rectangular patch antenna with multiple slots has been studied and investigated in this research article. The antenna is made of 1.0mm thick FR4 epoxy substrate. The antenna has a single-band peak centered at 39.03 GHz. The return loss value for the frequency band is -42.622dB, indicating good impedance matching and high efficiency and gain. Antenna design and power measurement is done using HFSS software. The required antenna size is 6.2×7.4×l.0mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, suitable for integration into small 5G devices. The company-recommended antenna provides excellent impedance performance with a partial impedance of 50 ohms and an imaginary impedance of 0 ohms. This document describes the evolution of the design and documents all enhancement techniques used and their impact on regression. Many parameters of the final model were analyzed, such as Return loss, gain, VSWR, interference coefficients, 2D radiation patterns, far field radiation, and 3D polar plot.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Denoising Anomaly Detection and Localisation Using BiGRU in Optical Fiber Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Efficient data transmission in optical fiber networks demands robust fault detection and classification. Leveraging Denoising Convolutional Autoencoder (DCAE) for fault detection and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) for classification, our method achieves a 96% efficiency rate. By accurately identifying anomalies like bad splices, dirty connectors, cuts, and eavesdropping, it ensures network integrity and confidentiality. This approach mitigates financial losses and potential disruptions caused by signal loss and interference. Overall, it provides a reliable solution for safe and steady communication in high- bandwidth optical networks.

articleTitle: Optimization of Dielectric Modulated TFET as a Label free Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work presents a label-free biosensor based on tunnel field effect transistors and using the concepts of dielectric modulation and charge plasma. Material from the gate oxide underlying the source electrode is removed for the nanogap cavity's creation, the biomolecules of interest are modelled within the nanogap cavity. Hereditary characteristics of the biomolecules, like the dielectric constant and charge density are used to identify them. The presence of a biomolecule within the nanogap cavity modifies the device's capacitance, electric field, and electrostatic potential, which in turn modifies the threshold voltage and drain current. Through the measurement of the drain current and threshold voltage change, the device's sensitivity is assessed. Using a low bandgap material result in a reduction in tunnelling width and an increase in TFET ON current. The effectiveness of the suggested devices is examined with respect to band energy, electric field, and sensitivity at various biomolecule dielectric constant (K) values. In addition to being label-free biosensors, the proposed devices have low heat budgets, are compatible with silicon technology, and are free from random dopant fluctuation.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Attention Approach for Diagnosis of Rice Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Rice diseases pose a major threat to the volume of crops and food security. It is especially vital to identify them at the early stage to apply effective management and prevention tactics. In this respect, convolutional neural networks (CNN), have been increasingly used due to their ability to automate the process of disease detection. In this paper, we combine attention mechanism to CNN to further improve the disease prediction. Experiment on rice disease dataset suggests the best results in terms of performance (93% accuracy) compare to prior methods.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition using YOLO based Deep Learning Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Understanding facial expressions is key to successful communication. It's like decoding a secret language that helps us know if someone is happy, sad, angry, surprised, or something else altogether. Harnessing facial emotion recognition (FER) in machines holds the potential to revolutionize human-computer interaction, improve customer service experiences and provide invaluable support in medical diagnosis. Machines can comprehend human's needs more effectively by reading the emotions from their facial expression and therefore this results in a more natural conversation between them and the machine. Various machine and deep learning methodologies have been implemented for FER. In this research work, the authors propose the state-of-the-art YOLO (You Only Look Once) based deep learning classifier for FER. The YOLO algorithm is a single-shot approach that efficiently classifies objects in a single pass. It achieves this by using a single neural network to predict bounding boxes and target class probabilities by utilizing the entire image as input. YOLOv8 is a recent iteration of the YOLO object detection algorithm is popular for its speed and accuracy which offers improvements over prior versions, making it a suitable choice for real-time intended task of FER. With the proposed classifier, the authors achieved test accuracy of 72.56% on the FER-2013 dataset in a seven-class FER task.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis for Modeling Copper Indium Gallium Selenide-based Solar Cells with Varying Absorber Layer Defect Density
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The semiconductors used to construct solar cells are the result of extensive research and development efforts. Currently, the substrate of choice is photovoltaic (PV) cells manufactured from silicon (Si), which accounts for more than 80% of global production. Due to their costly operation and production process, other compounds based on the CIS family seem superior to Si. Certain materials may largely absorb the sun's rays. In addition, CIGS has reached a new level of efficiency; it is with these materials that thin-film technologies can achieve their peak PCE. To maximize the efficiency of photovoltaic cells, use the SCAPS tool. This research takes CIGS-based PV cells and steps up or down the bulk defect density (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>) by 8 equal amounts, from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. The PV performance measures show a clear improvement at a fault level of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. A 22.90% PCE, 0.64V Voc, 82.9% FF, and 43.01 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Jsc are all present. The importance of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>on solar cells is highlighted by these results, which provide useful information for the development and improvement of CIGS-based PV cells. This abstract highlight the innovative elements of your study, particularly the systematic enhancement of defect density in CIGS-based PV cells and its substantial influence on enhancing their efficiency.

articleTitle: Routing Protocols Characterization in Real-World Vehicular Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Along with the growth of the automotive industry, Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) have also become popular in connecting vehicles. ITS plays an essential role in improving road safety and security, as well as the efficiency and reliability of road networks and traffic. One of the essential components of ITS is VANET. In this, the drivers can be alerted beforehand about intersection alerts, congestion alerts, emergency vehicle alerts, and junction alerts. This paper gives real-world scenario simulation research on vehicle-to-vehicle connectivity and vehicle-to-roadside unit via different routing protocols in VANET to analyze KIPs parameters like throughput, delay, and jitter on different number of vehicular nodes. The simulation is performed using the NetSim network simulator, which examines behavior and performance.

articleTitle: FPGA Based LSTM Network: A Power and Resource Optimized Solution for Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: LSTM, a recurrent neural network (RNN) well-suited for sequential data tasks, often incurs computational expenses during training and deployment, particularly with large and intricate models. The enhancement of LSTM network performance can be accomplished through hardware acceleration. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), enabling custom circuit implementation, can facilitate the creation of hardware accelerators for LSTM networks, resulting in substantial speed improvements over software implementations. An LSTM network hardware accelerator was implemented on the ZedBoard, a well-known FPGA development board. Performance evaluations of this accelerator across various time series datasets were conducted. The results demonstrated that the proposed accelerator achieved speedups of up to 45x compared to the software implementation. The accelerator's performance is on par with leading LSTM accelerators implemented on other FPGA platforms. The accelerator attains a performance level of 1.203 GOP/S while operating within a power consumption of 0.235W, making it well-suited for power-constrained applications.

articleTitle: Triple Band Microstrip Planar Antenna with DGS for WiMAX (3.5 GHz / 6.5 GHz) and C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The proposal and investigation of a triple band microstrip planar antenna for triple-frequency multiband operation have been carried out. The antenna employs a defective ground structure, incorporating three rectangular patches, each of a specified size 28.5 mm x 3.2 mm. The designed antenna features a compact overall size of 29.01 × 34.95 × 1.6 mm and operates within the frequency ranges of 3.5 GHz / 6.5 GHz, making it suitable for WiMAX and C band applications. Electromagnetic energy is coupled to the radiator through a compact microstrip feedline using a lumped port. In this FR4 epoxy substrate with a thickness of 1.6mm and a dielectric constant of 4.4, the antenna is designed. The proposed antennas exhibit return losses of -28.6414 / -24.3972 / -20.4478 dB, on three resonated frequencies 3.5 / 4.7 / 6.5 GHz, respectively. Using HFSS, we design and analyze the antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Canonical Huffman Encoder in VLSI for Data Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Design of Canonical Huffman Encoder is an emerging technology in Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI). The proposed design comprises three key stages: Frequency Generation, Code Size Computing, and Sorting and Code Size Limiting. This canonical Huffman encoding approach assigns variable length codes to symbols according to their frequencies, simplifying the encoding process. This frequency data constructing a canonical Huffman tree, optimizing binary codes for symbols and effectively reducing the overall data sizes. When implemented in Verilog 2017.4, it generates encoding bits as output, representing canonical code-sizes and canonical code-words. The results indicated that the proposed architecture decreased encoding time by 46.09%. Furthermore, a reduction in area of 60% and a power saving of 70% were observed in the Huffman encoder. The hardware implementation of LZ77 encoder and dynamic huffman encoder in data compression are designed for effective implementation of GZIP compression. Above the scenario has been executed using the Nexys A7-100T Artix-7 Series FPGA Evaluation Board. GZIP, an extensively utilized compression algorithm recognized for its effective compression ratios, is targeted to achieve a compression ratio of 88.92%.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization on Accurate Trajectory of Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: For systems to act efficiently, there has to be good enough control over the system to achieve desired behavior. The tracking trajectory is one characteristic that comes into the picture while analyzing a particular system's efficiency. Thus, there has to be a focus on achieving minimum error while tracking the trajectory. Henceforth, further approaches have been discussed in order to achieve the same. Moving on, the first approach gives a deeper dive into the mathematical and physics-based approach where error variation in 2-D Planar objects is compared with 3-D Planar objects. At the same time, the setbacks have been presented and a deep discussion involving robot dynamics has been explored in order to overcome the same. In further quest to improve its efficiency, proportional-integral-derivative controllers, classic Ziegler-Nichols method, and metaheuristic algorithm-based approach like Ant Colony Optimization are explored.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Nitrides with Group III based Semiconductor in JLTFET Device
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work presents a numerical analysis of nitride (group V) material with group III materials to make a compound semiconductor material are being used as a body material in junctionless tunnel field-effect-transistor (JLTFET). The semiconductor material that has been used in the body of the JLTFET device are AlN, GaN, and InN. The compound semiconductor materials are mostly wide bandgap materials that has higher mobility than silicon material. The comparative analysis has been carried out considering several figures-of-merits like transfer characteristics, potential distribution profile, bandgap fluctuations, electric field drop, and electron concentrations. Futhermore, the electron concentration and potential drop across the channel have been examined by plotting the contour diagram of the device.

articleTitle: Enhanced LEACH for Improving Lifespan of Hierarchical Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: One of the most often chosen services for use in the technical sector, in applications in industries, or in the marketplace is wireless sensor networks. Important considerations when developing suitable sensor network wireless routing algorithms is energy required to transport data from sensor's node to their destination. In this paper, an improvised version of “Low energy adaptive clustering hierarchy” called Enhanced LEACH is proposed. It defies limitations of traditional LEACH and enhances lifespan of the network. LEACH does not allow the sensor nodes which had been cluster heads in the previous rounds despite having energy beyond the threshold value. Enhanced LEACH allows all sensor nodes to participate in cluster head election technique by not differentiating sensor nodes which were selected as cluster nodes in previous rounds. Thereby considering sensor nodes based on their energy remaining in election of cluster head. Simulation results obtained has a clear advantage for proposed protocol in terms of dead nodes and packets delivered to base station and cluster heads.

articleTitle: Internal Defect Detection in Mango X-ray Images using Image Processing and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The mango seed weevil is found in the world's major mango-producing regions and causes significant economic losses in mango fruit production. Many nations have identified the mango seed weevil as a dangerous quarantine pest, and its presence in exported mangoes can lead to the rejection of entire cargoes to stop the pest from spreading into mango-producing nations. It can also cause decreased seed germination, fruit pulp damage, and early fruit drop in mangoes. To prevent this menace, non-destructive evaluation methods need to be developed to detect the presence of seed weevils without cutting the mango fruit. A non-destructive method makes it possible to identify infested mangoes before they reach the market or processing facilities. This early detection helps prevent the spread of infestation, reducing overall fruit loss. For this experiment, 55 healthy mangoes and 5 defective mango samples were used in this work. A pipeline has been developed using image processing and machine learning-based techniques to process the X-ray scans of mangoes, automatically detect the presence of seed weevils inside the fruit, and display the final result on the screen. It also generates an imprint of the inner seed profile, depicting the presence of the infection inside it. In identifying the defective and normal samples, a 94% accuracy rate was achieved. At the end of the scan of mango samples, the generated report includes internal defect details regarding the seed weevil defect presence and its location in the mango sample.

articleTitle: Early Intervention in Cardiology Using SVM for Heart Failure Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study's predictive modelling is based on the support vector machine (SVM) technique, which is well-suited to dealing with large amounts of complicated health data. Considering how hectic life is for the majority of us now, it's hard to believe that more people back then had truly weak hearts. When cardiac function declines to an abnormal level, the condition is known as heart failure. When it comes to determining who is at risk for major vascular problems and when those problems could manifest, SVM is a lifesaver. The SVM's classification skills have an impressive 79% accuracy rate, which is applicable to many clinical indications and risk factors. This is just remarkable. Now it's very evident that real physicians can revolutionise healthcare by detecting cardiac problems early on with the help of these forecasts. Along the way, they can also reduce healthcare costs. The importance of utilising intelligent, well-informed computer algorithms to detect and treat heart failure at an early stage is highlighted in this work, which also paves the way for improved health monitoring strategies.

articleTitle: FPGA-Optimized Asymmetrical and Symmetrical Six-Term Karatsuba Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The need for efficient multiplication of large integer polynomials in contemporary cryptographic systems is crucial. This study explores six-term Karatsuba multiplication, known for its efficiency but often avoided due to complex sub-multiplications. The focus is on implementing asymmetrical and symmetrical six-term Karatsuba Multiplication (ASTKM-I, ASTKM-II, SSTKM-I, and SSTKM-II) for enhanced speed and hardware utilization. To evaluate performance, Area-Time-Product (ATP) is calculated and compared with conventional asymmetrical and symmetrical six-term Karatsuba multiplication (CASTKM and CSSTKM) and state-of-the-art approaches. Hardware implementations on a Virtex-7 FPGA device in Xilinx ISE platform show that the best proposed method (ASTKM-II) outperforms other designs, being 17.983%, 79.361 %, 33.439%, 3.536%, 41.494%, 5.975%, and 9.343% better than Direct Multiplication (DM), Traditional Schoolbook Multiplication (Traditional SBM), CASKTM, ASKTM-I, CSSTKM, SSTKM-I, and SSTKM-II, respectively, for 1024-bit inputs.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Area Efficient Adaptive Filter for Low Computational Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The proposed work is based on the reduction of computational complexity as well as chip area for an adaptive filter architecture using the sign-sign least mean square (LMS) algorithm. The computations required for the sign-sign LMS algorithm have been reduced significantly compared to the standard least mean square (LMS) algorithm as the proposed method does not require any multiplier in the weight update loop. We have designed two filters for our proposed design, the first being a normal FIR filter and the other pipelined FIR filter, which uses pipelining techniques to achieve better throughput and the weights of the filter updates according to the proposed algorithm. The synthesis and implementation of the design have been done on the Xilinx Vivado tool using Verilog hardware description language (HDL), and the utilization of hardware resources and timing reports have been compared for both cases and found that minimal increment in the hardware resources, the maximum frequency of operation of the filter can be increased. The designs are being realized using Xilinx Artix - 7 FPGA.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Pneumonia Detection: Enhanced Chest X-ray Interpretation with CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The nearly lethal bacterial disease known as pneumonia, caused by the streptococcus pneumoniae bacterium, can infect any individual at any time. It often affects one or both lungs. One out of every three deaths in India is attributed to pneumonia, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO). In order to diagnose pneumonia, chest X-rays must be reviewed by trained radiologists. In order to treat pneumonia as quickly as possible, especially in faraway regions, it would be beneficial to have an automated method to detect the disease. The success of deep learning algorithms in analysing medical images has piqued a lot of people's interest in using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for illness detection. The proposed CNN-based method has several advantages over more traditional approaches, including greater accuracy, scalability, and the possibility of automation. Our proposal aims to improve the accuracy of pneumonia diagnoses by using deep learning techniques to identify complex patterns and traits in medical imaging data. Furthermore, features extracted from large datasets using pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) models perform quite well in image classification tasks. In this study, we evaluate these models’ capacity to distinguish between normal and pathological chest X-rays by employing pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) models as feature extractors and a number of classifiers thereafter. Analytical methods are employed to determine which CNN model is most suitable for the job at hand.

articleTitle: Distributed Denial of Service Attack Mitigation Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: A Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack poses a significant threat by inundating a target with a deluge of traffic, rendering its services inaccessible. In response to this menace, reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a promising avenue for effectively detecting and mitigating DDoS attacks within a simulated environment. Central to this approach is the utilization of a controller, which dynamically manages network resources while integrating feedback from the environment. Through RL, the system develops an adaptive detection policy, leveraging insights gleaned from analyzing pertinent traffic features in packet flow data. RL agent is trained to discern between benign and malicious traffic, with the overarching goal of maximizing cumulative rewards over time. Upon detection of a DDoS attack, the controller orchestrates a suite of mitigation strategies, thereby safeguarding the integrity and availability of the network. This paper delves into the intricate workings of this RL-based approach, elucidating its efficacy in fortifying network defenses against the pernicious threat of DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Temperature Compensated Read Assist Circuit to Enhance SNM of 6T SRAM in 18FDSOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this paper a SRAM read assist circuit in 18nm FD-SOI technology using temperature-compensated word lineunderdrive (WLUD) is presented that can increase the dynamic noise margin of selected bit cells. This enhances stability during read operation at higher temperatures (at higher temperatures, noise margin is low). The proposed temperature-compensatedread assist circuit improves read stability by reducing the appliedgate voltage on the pass gates of SRAM bit cells. The amount of WLUD depends on the temperature and process variations, the readability of the selected cell will also be function of temperature,the power loss during read operation of the proposed method is also reduced as compared to previous, constant underdrive circuits up to some extent due to continuous current flowing through supply to ground during read assist. The proposed temperature-compensated read-assist method can achieve a higher sigma qualification than fixed underdrive circuits and which degrades performance at other than worst corners. The measurement result using 18-nm FDSOI technology indicates thatthe proposed temperature-compensated read assist circuit can operate without any failure up to 12% underdrive.

articleTitle: An Assessment of the Operation of Hybrid FSO/RF DF Relayed Satellite Communication Network Using Pulse Position Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research paper introduces a novel strategy aimed at addressing communication challenges in demanding environments, focusing on improving the efficacy of utilizing By combining a hybrid Free-Space Optical (FSO) and Radio Frequency (RF) method, HAPS functions as a decode and forward relay system. Across a wide range of applications, dependable and fast data transfer is essential in today's communication networks. The goal of the hybrid FSO/RF network is to address the inherent flaws in radio frequency and free-space communication technologies. The suggested solution creates a flexible backbone by combining a Decode and Forward relay, improving the performance of the entire system. This approach seeks to enable effective communication in situations where traditional systems might not be able to meet all of the needs. The results for BER and outage probability are calculated and studied using MATLAB. The paper emphasizes the significance of the hybrid approach as well as the PPM modulation technique in addressing challenges in satellite communication within demanding environments.

articleTitle: Spectrum Assignment in 5G and Beyond Ultra-Dense Networks Utilizing Deep Neural Network Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Extremely high throughput and data rates can be achieved with ultra-dense networks (UDN). However, the wide-ranging and random deployment of small base stations (SBSs) causes significant interference. A key issue is how to distribute cellular resources among small-cell user equipments (SUEs) in an effective manner to enhance the performance of these mobile services. One of the most significant challenges is figuring out how to distribute cellular resources across network users in a way that maximizes performance for these mobile applications. The generative adversarial networks double deep Q-network (GAN-DDQN) strategy has been proposed as a means of overcoming interference and obtaining effective energy-efficient resource allocation. To mitigate the impact of widely varying utility values, we propose a reward-clipping strategy for GAN-DDQN training. In a simulated setup, the suggested plan is assessed. The suggested strategy considerably increases energy efficiency, SINR, and throughput, as the numerical and simulation findings confirm.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Antimony with Group III Compounded Semiconductor Based JLTFET
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This report deals with the impact of compound semiconductor material where antimony (group V) material has been mixed with group III materials i.e., aluminum, gallium, and indium on junctionless tunnel field-effect transistor (JLTFET). A performance comparison has been done to understand the impact of increasing higher or lower bandgap material on the electrical performance of the device. The comparative analysis has been carried out considering several figures-of-merits like potential distribution profile, bandgap fluctuations, electric field profile, electron concentration, and the transfer characteristics of the device. The report also shows the contour diagram of potential drop and electron concentration distribution along the channel of the device.

articleTitle: ATP-Optimized Four-Term Karatsuba Multipliers for Large Integer Arithmetic on FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work presents two methods of hardware implementation of area-time-product (ATP)-optimized four-term Karatsuba multipliers (FTKM) on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). This is done by eliminating the effects of complexity of sub-multiplications present at the intermediate steps of computation. Besides these, hardware implementation of the proposed work suggests that the proposed FTKM multiplication methods (FTKM-I and FTKM-II) performs better in terms of resource utilization and delay minimization compared to other existing state-of-the-art multiplication methods, irrespective of input bit lengths. Hardware implementations of the proposed FTKM methods (FTKM-I and FTKM-II) multiplication architecture are demonstrated on a Virtex-7 FPGA device in Xilinx ISE platform. Here, the hardware implementation of the proposed FTKM multipliers is carried out for 128 bits, 256 bits, 512 bits, and 1024 bits, showcasing advantages in area-time-product (ATP) over previous research. ATP serves as the Figure-of-Merit (FoM) for determining the performance of the design.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 16-bit Modified Vedic Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In digital signal processing, the fast and highperforming Vedic multiplier (VM) is employed. Sixteen sutras, or formulas, form the foundation of Vedic multiplication. The multiplication of two numbers in this work is done using the Urdhva Tiryagbhyam (UT) sutra. This paper presents a modified Vedic multiplier (VM) which provides high computational speed, low power consumption, and minimal space requirements as an extra bonus. The Xilinx 14.7 software tool is used to design a 16-bit modified Vedic multiplier. The results are compared with VMs based on Carry-Save Adders (CSA) in terms of power usage, area, and delay. These parameters’ comparison shows that the updated multiplier offers significant improvements.

articleTitle: Exploring MOSFET Differential Amplifiers: Using TCAD and Multisim Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The investigation is conducted on the Silicon gate all around (Si-GAA) MOSFET with the help of 3D-ATLAS TCAD simulator. For the amplification purpose a differential amplifier is designed using Multisim by utilizing the parameters found from the above simulated model. It is found that the prosed model shows good amplification as compared to the inbuilt MOSFET model preset in Multisim simulator.

articleTitle: Design of Vertical Double Source TFET for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The design and analysis of a VDSTFET optimized for low power applications are presented in this paper. TFETs have attracted a lot of attention lately because of their ability for resolving problems with energy efficiency in contemporary integrated circuits. But ordinary TFET designs challenge to achieve low off-currents as well as high on-currents, which are essential for low power operations. This work suggests a unique VDS-TFET design that is low power application-optimized in response. By utilizing a vertical channel layout with two source regions, the suggested VDS-TFET design improves carrier injecting performance and electrostatic control. The design provides enhanced efficiency measures, such as steeper sub-threshold slopes, lower leakage currents, and increased oncurrents—all crucial for low power operation— through extensive devices simulations and improvement methodologies.

articleTitle: A Low Temperature Coefficient CMOS Voltage Reference for Wide Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper presents a wide temperature range CMOS voltage reference without BJT or passive resistors. The proposed CMOS voltage reference includes two voltage references and a temperature compensation circuit to attain a low-temperature coefficient across an extensive temperature range. The proposed voltage reference is implemented on 0.18 μm CMOS technology. The outcomes of the simulation illustrate that the proposed circuit operates across an extensive range of temperatures from −40°C to 200°C, exhibiting a temperature coefficient of 14.5 ppm/°C. The reference voltage is 465.66 mV at 0.9V. It is computed that the line sensitivity is 0.14%/V and power consumption is 5.6μW. The power supply rejection ratio is observed to be −35.77 dB within the frequency range of 1 Hz to 100 KHz. Output noise levels of 0.32 μ V/√Hz and 0.2 μ V/√Hz are obtained at frequencies of 100 KHz and 1 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis: A Machine Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: An essential part of natural language processing, sentiment analysis makes it possible to automatically extract sentiment from textual input. In this work, we examine how well different machine learning algorithms perform when used to analyze the sentiment of real-time Amazon reviews in the automobile niche. Leveraging a dataset comprising reviews from Amazon users, we employ SVM, KNN, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest algorithms to categorize text sentiment as positive, negative, or neutral. This work evaluates the performance of each algorithm in sentiment analysis tasks using strict evaluation standards and testing. Our findings provide insights into the effectiveness of machine learning approaches for analyzing sentiment in real-time reviews, offering valuable implications for businesses and organizations aiming to leverage customer feedback for decision-making and user experience enhancement.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of High-Speed, Low-Power Flash ADC for Mixed Signal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Nowadays modern semiconductor devices and system-on-chip (SoC)'s has mixed signal (Intellectual Property (IP)'s. So, a device is required which can convert one form of data into another form. ADC serves as a bridge between the analog world (sensor capturing real-world signals) and digital processing units. This research presents a detailed design methodology for a Flash-type ADC, utilizing the collaborative capabilities of Cadence for analog circuit design, SPICE for electrical simulation, and System Verilog with Real Number Modeling (RNM) for digital verification. The research focuses on the architectural optimization of a flash ADC, targeting enhancements in speed, power and efficiency by utilizing the suitable comparator. Furthermore, a reference voltage ladder is also designed to achieve high precision. The digital encoding logic, a vital component for translating comparator outputs into binary code is designed using System Verilog and modeled with RNM. Extensive simulations conducted in the Cadence environment, corroborated by SPICE analyses, demonstrate the ADC's robust performance, confirming its potential for deployment in high-speed applications such as digital communication, Mixed signal IPs, and instrumentation. The research culminates with a comprehensive evaluation of the ADC's performance metrics including Resolution, speed, and power consumption, highlighting its competitive edge in the ADC landscape.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and Gain Enhancement of a Rectangular Metasurface Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Antenna designers often deal with the trade-off between gain and bandwidth. This paper presents a novel technique based on metasurface reflector to enhance the gain and bandwidth of a rectangular microstrip patch antenna. The proposed rectangular patch antenna is designed with a resonant frequency of 2.4 GHz with FR4 substrate and partial ground plane. Partial ground plane is a well known technique for ultra wide band antenna applications. However, it reduces the gain of a patch antenna, remarkably. In order to increase the gain, a metasurface designed with elongated microstrip dipoles of length equal to Ag with FR4 substrate that is placed below the partial ground plane with a gap of λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/10. Simulated results obtained through ANSYS HFSS demonstrates an improvement in the gain from 2.4 dB to 5 dB with a bandwidth of about 2.5 times larger than the ordinary microstrip patch antenna of the same specifications. Simulated results have verifiedt that the overall performance of the microstrip antenna has been increased due to the metasurface reflector.

articleTitle: Automated Signature Verification in Bank Cheque Processing Using Siamese and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Bank cheques play a pivotal role in global financial transactions, with a vast number of them, processed daily. The conventional manual verification process, involving visual scrutiny of crucial details, is both time-consuming and labour-intensive, often leading to delays in transaction validation. This paper proposes an automated signature verification method for bank cheques, leveraging advancements in image processing and machine learning. Our approach begins with capturing a customer's handwritten signatures from cheque leaves. Our method outlines the various processing steps, including grayscale binarization, signature detection using OCR and Linesweep, and classification using SNN.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Link Adaptation on an Underwater Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication (UAC) networks face significant challenges due to rapid spatial and temporal variations in channel conditions influenced by environmental factors. To enhance system efficiency, adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) can be employed to adjust transmission parameters in response to these channel variations. A thorough analysis of a measured sea trial dataset is essential to determine an appropriate link adaptation strategy tailored to channel quality. This analysis employs a rule-based approach that includes three-dimensional evaluation, modulation-specific analysis, and fixed-SNR strategy. However, non-reversible nature of the rule-based strategy presents limitations, prompting an extension of the study to incorporate machine learning (ML) algorithms for classifying modulation levels and coding rate levels based on channel characteristics. Among four ML algorithms evaluated, the boosted regression tree (BRT) algorithm demonstrated exceptional accuracy, achieving a 99.97% success rate in MCS level classification. Further ML analysis involved various parameter combinations to classify coding rates, assessing both individual and overall classification accuracies. Additionally, the rule-based strategy was utilized to determine optimal threshold values for coding rate labels. This was achieved through the analysis of Gaussian distribution plots and multi-dimensional scatter plots, providing a comprehensive approach to link adaptation in UAC networks.

articleTitle: Comparison of Analog Performance between Si Junctionless FinFET, Si Conventional FinFET, Tunnel FET, and InGaAs MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The following article presents a comparative analysis of the analog performance amid Si junctionless (JL) FinFET, traditional inversion-mode (IM) FinFET, Tunnel FET, and InGaAs MOSFET. To do this work, a numerical device simulator has been applied. Our investigation reveals that although InGaAs MOSFET shows highest transconductance, particularly at higher VGS, TFET produces the highest intrinsic gain at relatively lower VGS values. Even though its transconductance is lower, JL FinFET produces the highest gain at higher VGS values due to its low drain conductance in spite of its low transconductance.

articleTitle: Study of Performance of Hybrid Satellite Terrestrial Cooperative Communication System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This review paper brings forward the hybrid satellite-terrestrial (HST) network applications based on Free Space Optical (FSO) communication. In particular, it highlights signal transmission, via amplifying and forward (AF) relaying in a satellite-terrestrial network. Additionally, transmission received by the user via direct link, relays, reflected broadcast, or FSO link is often masked by in-path barriers. The terrestrial connection follows Nakagami-m fading whereas, the FSO link between the relay and destination follows the gamma-gamma distribution. The satellite-relay and satellite-destination links are supposed to follow Shadowed-Rician fading. The Average rate of Symbol Error of the considered AF co-operative scheme for M-ary phase shift keying constellation method under consideration. In this review paper, we review the part of the maximum instant signal-noise ratio (SNR) of satellite-relay Earth station (ES) connection links and SNR at destination ES. We examine how elevation angles affect the SSK-assisted satellite communication system's channel capacity, diversity order, and SER performance.

articleTitle: ECG Data Compression Analysis by Employing Different Transforms in Orthogonal Transformation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Using the orthogonal transformation method, this paper presents the performance analysis of FFT, DHT, DCT, and DST for ECG data compression. When the heart muscle contracts or expands as a response to the command signals coming from electrical stimulus in its electro-conduction system, an ECG signal is generated. In today's fast-paced life, ECG data compression is essential as today's lifestyle leads to many health problems. More storage space is required for research purposes or data transmission, and data compression utilizes memory storage effectively. The performance of each transform has been recorded by calculating compression ratio (CR) to measure the compression acquired, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to measure signal strength to the background noise, and percent rms difference (PRD) for error measurement. The parameters have been measured using Python and has been compared with the literature. The Discrete Cosine transform performed well compared to the rest in the orthogonal transformation method with a PRD of 4.80 at CR of 5.14 and an SNR of 26.36.

articleTitle: Development and Simulation of Sierpinski Triangle Antenna for ISM Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-band, wide band, pla-nar fractal antenna based on Sierpinski triangle geometry. The antenna is simulated using Ansys HFSS (high-frequency structure simulator) software on a 1.6mm thick FR4 dielectric. The choice of thickness and dielectric is made keeping in mind the most commonly used materials for Printed Circuit Boards (PCB). A third iteration of Sierpinski triangle is on top side and a partial ground is used on the bottom side of the dielectric. The antenna thus implemented, has a dimension of 80mm x 85mm x 1.6mm. This antenna achieves -10dB return loss bandwidth for the frequencies 0.71-1.14 GHz, 2.32-2.75 GHz and 4.34-5.97 GHz. Thus, this antenna can operate in the most commonly used ISM band frequencies - 868MHz, 915MHz, 2.4GHz and 5.7GHz respectively. Gain Values of 0.6dB, 1.9dB and 2.7dB are obtained for 868MHz, 2.4GHz and 5.7GHz respectively. Radiation efficiency is higher than 80% for all the above mentioned frequencies. The Antenna is fabricated and tested partially using NanoVna. For the frequency range of testing done, the NanoVnaresult and simulation result agree well with each other.

articleTitle: Performance of Deep Embedded Clustering and Low-Complexity Greedy Algorithm for Power Allocation in NOMA-Based 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research probes a novel method of using Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access based Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) to enhance downlink communication in fifth-generation (5G) networks. It explores the comparison between two sub-channel allocation methods namely the Low-Complexity Greedy Algorithm and Deep embedded clustering algorithm using measures like achievable rate and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) calculated via Shannon's Capacity Theorem using Channel State Information (CSI), a dynamic power allocation technique. Simulation results verified through numerical evaluation show that proposed schemes can significantly increase the system capacity in a given scenario, creating new opportunities for advancements in wireless technology.

articleTitle: Dysarthria Voice Disorder Detection Using Mel Frequency Logarithmic Spectrogram and Deep Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Dysarthric speech recognition (DSR), often known as DSR, is an important tool that enables persons with vocal impairments to participate in voice-based automation systems and human-computer interaction. As a result of the poor intelligibility of handicapped speakers, the limited availability of datasets, and the low intra-class and inter-class variability in the speech samples, DSR is an essential component. This research provides a DSR based on the Mel Frequency Logarithmic Spectrogram (MFLS) and Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN). The suggested MFLS+DCNN offers an improved representation of the voice signal in terms of its spectral and temporal characteristics. The results of the MFLS-DCNN scheme are validated using the UASpeech dataset, which was developed based on accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score. With an accuracy of 96.83%, a recall performance of 0.97, a precision performance of 0.96, and an F1-score of 0.97, the scheme that is proposed has shown a considerable improvement above the conventional state-of-the-art.

Author Keywords: voice pathology are some of the topics that are being discussed

articleTitle: Melasma Segmentation using U-Net: A Precise Approach for Skin Pigment Disorder Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Skin serves as a physical barrier, protecting the body from potentially hazardous exterior elements. The skin can develop several disorders, but one of the most commonly occurring and hazardous is melasma. Brown to gray-brown spots on the face, especially on the cheekbones, nasal bridge, forehead, chin, and above the top lip, are the hallmarks of the common skin disorder melasma. Early detection of melasma facilitates timely management and intervention, which can help keep the problem from getting worse. There are a variety of techniques and treatments used to prevent and treat melasma, which include both conventional and modern approaches like deep learning and machine learning. The proposed solution for melasma detection uses U-net convolutional networks. This offers an efficient and scalable method for the early detection of melasma, allowing for individualized treatment plans. The accuracy of the system is 90.97%.

articleTitle: Automatic Number Plate Recognition in Hazy Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study explores automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) in hazy conditions, emphasizing the critical role of dehazing methods in enhancing model accuracy and resilience, especially in challenging weather scenarios like winter. Through a systematic evaluation of ANPR techniques, the study identifies effective dehazing strategies tailored to address specific environmental obstacles, underscoring the significance of customized approaches for optimal performance. By integrating the dark channel prior technique, the model's robustness in adverse weather conditions is significantly improved, laying the foundation for future advancements in ANPR technology through targeted research on hardware optimization and enhanced dehazing methodologies.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of Franckeite Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this study, we have designed the franckeite based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor. The sensitivity of the proposed sensor is directly influenced by the thickness of the franckeite layer, where franckeite is deposited onto a copper (Cu) layer surface. In theory, this configuration has attained a sensitivity of up to 271.25 °/RIU, which is 53.71% more sensitive than conventional sensors. Furthermore, we investigate the possibility of incorporating bilayer franckeite (2*franckeite) layers to improve biocompatibility and sensitivity to an even greater extent. The figure of merit (FoM) of 54.25/RIU is achieved. Also, utilized the proposed sensor to demonstrate the penetration depth (PD). The PD of 205.94nm is obtained. Since franckeite is a 2D material, we believe that it will benefit for the detection of biological and chemical sensing technologies.

articleTitle: Modelling and Performance Analysis of Non-Toxic MASnI3 Perovskite Solar Cell with 28.93% Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Recently, lead-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) grabbed the worldwide popularity in photovoltaic industry owing to its remarkable properties.
