Few challenges such as toxic elements, instability etc. restricts the use of inorganic-organic lead-based perovskite solar cells. To achieve these objectives inorganic-organic MASnI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> based solar cell with less toxicity is used as a light harvesting layer in the proposed structure. In this work, FTO/ TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ MASnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/ Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O/Au structure has been studied by SCAPS-1D simulation. By choosing the material TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> for electron transport layer (ETL) and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O for hole transport layer (HTL), it has been noticed that the cell performed better in comparison to previously existing structures. The characteristics such as thickness of light harvesting layer including electron and hole transport layer thickness, doping of different layers, operating temperature etc. have thoroughly been examined in relation to different characteristics of PSCs. As a result, maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) reached upto 28.93% along a FF = 88.9, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf> = 1.25 V, and Jsc = 25.89 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Hence, this work motivates the researchers to fabricate the high efficiency low-toxic PSCs in future.

articleTitle: Power Spectrum Estimation Method to Detect Target Frequency from SSVEP Brain Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The most critical and important issue is determining the target flicker from the steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain signal. SSVEP-based BCI technology is mainly utilized to control external devices by detecting the target frequency when the user concentrates on the visual flickering frequency. The effectiveness of several power spectrum estimating (PSE) techniques for identifying SSVEP responses from recorded EEG time series data is evaluated by the authors in this work. The IMFs that fall in the range of target frequency are further passed through PSE methods for target frequency detection. Various PSE methods such as FFT, Welch, Burg, and Yule-walker are applied to plot the magnitude spectrum of corresponding IMFs. The performances of the proposed methods are evaluated using two online single-channel datasets. The recorded EEG signals contain the stimulus frequencies from 6Hz to 15.8Hz. The accuracy of detection of each SSVEP frequency was computed to evaluate the effectiveness of the recommended approach. The final results show that the proposed method EMD + Welch periodogram estimation method outperforms the other proposed methods EMD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+\text{FFT}$</tex>, EMD + Burg method, and EMD +Yul-walker.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power, Thermal, and Temperature Considerations in FPGA-Based Shift Register Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this paper critical issue of energy scarcity in digital circuits draws attention to the challenges related to shift register power consumption. It investigates how to use FPGA families and Xilinx Vivado software to optimize power consumption without compromising functionality. Energy shortage is addressed by innovative methods based on extensive experimentation and analysis that offer practical solutions for creating energy-efficient circuits in FPGA systems. This paper provides useful information for lowering power consumption issues and clearing the road for resilient and sustainable digital systems.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 38GHz mmWave Modified MIMO Antenna on Low Permittivity Substrate for 5G Ka Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study focuses on the design of a two-port MIMO antenna operating at 38.00GHz in the Ka Band of FR2 in mmWave spectrum, designed using FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate. The single-element of this 2-Port MIMO antenna occupy a volume of 6.2×7.4×l.0mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(L×W×H). The single element design is enhanced using two rectangular slots on the rectangular patch and the ground plane on the opposite side is enhanced using a circular slot, enabling resonance of this enhanced single element at 39.00GHz. The compact two-port MIMO antenna is designed using this single element structure with a total volume of 6.2xl0.4xl.0mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(LxWxH) and an inter-element spacing of 2.70mm. The optimization through parametric analysis and enhancement by creating two additional rectangular slots on the ground element are used to reach narrow-bandwidth characteristics with high impedance matching achieved at 38.00GHz. The rectangular patch has a dimension 3.5×2.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The enhanced 2-Port MIMO antenna demonstrates a peak gain of 4.02dBi and a radiation efficiency of 91% at the resonant frequency(38.00GHz), while maintaining a stable radiation pattern in E and H plane. Diversity performance analysis of enhanced 2-Port MIMO provides <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ECC}_{38.00\text{GHz}} < 0.0075,\text{DG}_{38.00\text{GKz}} > 9.9996,\text{TARC}_{38.00\text{GHz}}=-20.25\text{dB}$</tex>, MEG1- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MEG}_{28.00\text{GHz}} < 0.40\text{db})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CCL}_{38.00\text{GHz}} < 0.25\mathrm{b}/\sec/\text{Hz}$</tex> in proposed bandwidth, indicating its suitability for compact 5G devices in Ka band applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Subject Specific Model and General Model using Bayesian Algorithm and Compare their Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) signals play a pivotal role in numerous applications, offering insights into muscle activity crucial for various fields. However, the challenge lies in mitigating noise interference during transmission, which significantly impacts signal accuracy and reliability. To address this pressing issue, our research delves into the efficacy of subject-specific and general-specific models for EMG signal detection, employing sophisticated Bayesian Inference algorithms. This comprehensive investigation encompasses a diverse dataset representing various demographics, including healthy individuals, older adults, and individuals with specific medical conditions. By leveraging this rich dataset, we aim to conduct a robust evaluation of the proposed models, shedding light on their performance across different population segments and scenarios. The overarching goal of this research is to advance the field of EMG signal detection, with profound implications for neuromuscular diagnosis, prosthetic control systems, and the de-velopment of intuitive human-computer interfaces. By enhancing our understanding of EMG signal processing and modeling, we strive to pave the way for innovative solutions that empower individuals with improved healthcare diagnostics and assistive technologies, ultimately enhancing their quality of life.

articleTitle: Low Power and High-Speed Current Mirror Based Level Shifter in Sub-Threshold Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work depicts a low power and high-speed current mirror-based level shifter that operates in sub-threshold regime for different voltage domain blocks. The proposed technique eliminates the static current leakage by incorporating the leakage control transistors in the output split input inverter. In addition to that it employs devices with different sizing and multi-threshold cells in order to achieve low power and operates well in sub-threshold regime. This work has been implemented in gpdk90 nm process node which confirms that the level shifter can transform input voltage as low as 0.4V at 1MHz to 1.2V. The power and the delay for the proposed circuit at an input voltage level of 0.4 V/1MHz to an output voltage level of 1.2 V is 41.98 nW and 5.85 ns, respectively.

Author Keywords: split input inverter and leakage control transistors

articleTitle: MOSFET Based Different Structures for Hydrogen Sensor Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The innovations and use of FET for hydrogen sensing application has been tremendously increasing and found its great use in production industries. Leakage of hydrogen is fatal, as contains hydrogen which when inhaled, mixes with oxygen of the body and hence creates scarcity of oxygen, leading to loss of life. So, its timely detection using advanced devices with high sensitivity is very crucial. Since a long time, various structures have been modelled with scaling in devices, to cope up the existing limitations of model. In this paper, different device structures are shown that are used as hydrogen sensor are analyzed.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for EEG-Based Motor Imagery Classification Across Diverse Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The BRAIN CONTROL INTERFACE(BCI) introduce a different framework for human-computer interaction, enabling diverse applications across various fields. Motor imagery (MI) based BCI has found widespread application in assisting individuals with paralysis by controlling prosthetic limbs, smart homes, and even virtual reality experiences. Despite these ad-vancements, there are still limitations and obstacles to overcome before BCI technology can be widely adopted. This article focuses on a critical aspect of BCI development: accurately classifying MI tasks. The research focuses on the effectiveness of the EEGNet model for classifying MI signals. The findings highlight a significant difference in EEGNet's performance across various datasets on the BCI Competition IV. Notably, the model achieved accuracies of 85.74% and 69.68% for subject-specific scenarios on BCI-Competition IV-2b and IV-2a datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Adiabatic Logic-Based Multiplexer and Full Adder Circuits for Ultra-Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In the current scenarios, power dissipation is the primary concern when designing a VLSI circuit. The need for logic devices that use minimal power is continually growing, and adiabatic logic provides an ideal answer to this problem. The adiabatic technique is a prominent approach that significantly reduces power dissipation by recycling the stored charge at different nodes. Since the multiplexer plays a significant role in data transmission, whereas a full adder is needed for many arithmetic operations, an efficient low-power design circuit is required for these operations. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of traditional CMOS, traditional Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic (PFAL), and various modified PFAL circuits for 2:1 multiplexer and full adder circuits. These circuits were implemented and simulated by 90nm and 45nm technology using the Cadence virtuoso EDA tool, and the average power dissipation and performance for each of the circuits were observed. This design showcased in this research holds potential for various applications, such as portable devices, low-frequency operating systems, battery-powered systems, and high-performance computing systems.

articleTitle: Computational Study on the Effect of CdS Buffer Layer in an Environmentally Safe CuSCN based Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) is used to conduct extensive research on the design of perovskite solar cells based on hybrid metal halide (CH3NH3SnI3), with the goal of increasing their energy conversion capability. The proposed device (ITO/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CdS/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CuSCN/Au) performance has been explored by optimizing the design variables like temperature (280K to 330K) and absorber layer thickness (750nm to 1300nm). Moreover, the impact of cadmium sulfide, ‘CdS’ as buffer layer is also studied. An analysis has been conducted in order to ascertain the best composition of the device's layers for optimal performance. These layers include the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>as absorber/active layer, copper (I) thiocyanate (CuSCN) as hole transport layer (HTL), tin dioxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) for electron transport (ETL), and CdS for active buffering. At optimized temperature of 280K and thickness of 950nm, the open circuit voltage is 1.05V, fill factor is 87.44%, short circuit current density is 33.89mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and efficiency is 31.06%.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Fruit Crop Disease Classification Using Plants Leaf Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Agriculture plays an important role in the economy, providing nutrition, food, and livelihoods to billions of people in this world. Fruits are a vital component of a balanced diet, acting as a rich source of antioxidants, vitamins, minerals, and fibres. To ensure its proper supply to the market, early diagnosis and treatment of fruit crop disease can play a significant role. In order to make this process quicker and more accurate, Deep learning (DL) techniques can be of immense help. In the proposed study, the implementation of four DL models: Visual Geometry Group VGG16, VGG19, EfficientNet-B0, and MobileNet is done on a subset of the Plant Village database, constituting 7,233 leaf images of apples and grapes divided into 8 different classes. Evaluation is done through various metrics, namely Precision, Recall, F1-score and Specificity. All the DL models performed well by attaining accuracy above 95%. MobileNet performed best among all DL models by achieving an accuracy of 99.38%, while VGG16, VGG19, and EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 96.75%, 98.69% and 98.76% respectively.

articleTitle: Hair Loss Stage Prediction Using different CNN models
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Hair loss disorders are prevalent and present challenges in prompt and accurate diagnosis. Traditional diagnostic approaches, involving visual inspections and medical tests by dermatologists, often result in delays exacerbating the conditions. In response, a deep learning solution utilizing a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) was deployed to effectively predict various hair loss categories such as alopecia, psoriasis, and folliculitis. However, this endeavor encountered obstacles including limited access to datasets and the presence of diverse online images impacting the model's precision. In addition to the success of the model, a dataset was curated incorporating factors like SSB, aging, hierarchical characteristics, and stress, which holds promise for future investigations. The significance of this study lies in its contribution to timely identification of hair loss through neural network applications, benefiting both medical practitioners and affected individuals. The methodology of the project revolves around harnessing the capabilities of deep learning models to discern subtle patterns within frontal facial images. Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) facilitates automatic extraction and comprehension of relevant information from images, enabling the detection of minute variations in hair density, coverage, and distribution. These learned features serve as the groundwork for an accurate classification system aligning with the progressive stages of hair loss as defined by the Hamilton-Norwood scale. In summary, this research endeavors to demonstrate the efficacy of deep learning techniques in automatically identifying different stages of hair loss from frontal facial photos. By integrating neural networks and image processing expertise, the aim is to advance hair loss diagnosis and treatment methodologies, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for individuals affected by this condition

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Wireless Communication System with Dynamic Node Positioning Over Fisher-Snedecor F Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: New trends in futuristic communication technologies such as 5G and beyond allows wide range of ubiquitous coverage, D2D and M2M oriented point to point communication. These communication scenarios led to consideration of impact of user mobility over various wireless channels in both homogeneous as well as heterogeneous environments. The user mobility in 1D, 2D and 3D is accurately analyzed with change in user's perceived signal power using Random Way Mobility (RWP) model. Again, the Fisher Snedecor F fading model precisely modelled the above said communication scenarios at mm band for wireless network. The paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of dynamic node positioning over F fading channels under diverse mobility conditions. We derive the novel expression of probability density function and cumulative distribution function close form expression by incorporating RWP model. Then the obtained composite fading channel PDF and CDF are used to obtained performance matrices such as average bit error rate and outage probability for a mobile user in all the three-topologies. To validate our findings, we conduct a comprehensive Monte Carlo simulation across various configurations, showing excellent agreement with our results.

articleTitle: ASIC Implementation of FIR Filter Using 16x16 Hybrid Vedic-Dadda Multiplier for ECG-Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)

authors.preferredName: Sankula Sri Naga Sai Venkata Durga Prasad

abstract: As technology is scaling, the contemporary world is achieving the demand of replacing the existing systems by their area and power compatibility. Electrocardiography (ECG) is a biomedical device that is considered as a fundamental tool in diagnosing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). To build area and power-optimized biomedical devices that use basic blocks like multipliers, adders, filters, etc., need developed efficient basic blocks. This work proposes the design of a linear-phase low-pass FIR filter (LPFF), by employing a hybrid multiplier named the Hybrid Vedic Dadda multiplier. The LPFF is compared and proved to reduce area by 5.5%, power by 8.5%, delay by 2.2%, and saving EPT by around 9.5% compared with the existing Hybrid Vedic Wallace Tree Multiplier (HVWTM) FIR filter. The proposed FIR filter's efficiency is verified with Intel DSP Builder, followed by implementation and synthesis with the Cadence RTL compiler in 90nm technology.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Heuristic Approach Assisted Dynamic Spectrum Assignment with Fragmentation Minimization in EON-SDM
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Dynamic Core Allocation with Fragmentation Optimization is a vital aspect of spectrum management in contemporary communication networks. This paper introduces a new method that utilizes machine learning techniques, specifically deep learning with TensorFlow and Keras, to enhance core allocation and reduce fragmentation in the network. Weemploythe Dijkstra algorithm to ascertain the k shortest routes connecting a designated source and destination. Next, we calculate fragmentation coefficients using the Contiguous Aligned Slot Ratio (CASR) measure. Eventually, we utilize a deep learning model that has been trained using these fragmentation coefficients to forecast whether a core will be accepted or rejected, thus facilitating the allocation of cores in a dynamic manner. In addition, we present a function that calculates the Bandwidth Blocking Probability (BBP) in order to assess the effectiveness of the allocation technique. The findings suggest that our technique is effective in minimizing fragmentation and boosting spectrum utilization, resulting in lower BBP values and improved network performance.

articleTitle: Brain Signal-Based Emotion Classification Using DEAP Corpus
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The research paper presents a study on utilizing deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to classify emotions based on Electroencephalography (EEG) signals captured from the human brain using electrodes placed on the scalp. The study primarily analyses the DeapData corpus, employing advanced deep-learning techniques to interpret and classify emotional states from EEG readings. The LSTM model is utilized for its capability to capture long-term dependencies in sequential data, while the CNN model is harnessed for its effectiveness in extracting features from EEG brain signals. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach in accurately categorizing emotions from EEG brain signal data, emphasizing the potential of deep learning techniques in neuroimaging and affective computing applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Photovoltaic Performance of CIGS-based Solar Cells by Varying Their Thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) technology has garnered significant global interest because of its reputation as the most cost-effective solution for meeting the growing energy needs of the globe. CIGS (Copper Indium Gallium Selenide), indicates a specific kind of solar cell technology that utilizes thin-film materials. CIGS solar cells are produced by the deposition of a thin film of copper, indium, gallium, and selenium onto a substrate, which is often glass or a flexible substance such as metal or plastic foil. The CIGS solar cell has a superior absorption factor, over-time dependability, and inexpensive fabrication expense. The CIGS material has a modifiable bandgap that may be altered. This article presents research conducted on CIGS solar cells, focusing on ways to optimize efficiency via the use of “thickness variation”. The SCAPS-1D tool has been utilized for conducting computational simulations. The effectiveness of CIGS solar cells is examined using thickness variation from 0.06 to 0.6μm in 10 steps. Consequently, the findings presented in this publication are likely to generate increased interest among academics in the area, inspiring them to develop this structure and explore more avenues for enhancing its efficacy The highest PV metrics show the following values when the CIGS layer thickness is 600nm: PCE = 22.15%, Voc = 0.63 V, Jsc = 42.29 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and FF = 82.64%.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of FPGA-Optimized Asymmetrical Three-Term Karatsuba Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper focusses on FPGA-based optimized implementations of asymmetrical three-term Karatsuba multiplication (AThTKM) architecture. Two multiplications, AThTKM-I and AThTKM-II, are proposed to implement AThTKM, aimed at enhancing the critical path and circuit area. The performance of the proposed design methods is assessed by computing the Area-Time-Product (ATP) and comparing it with conventional asymmetrical three-term Karatsuba multiplication (CAThTKM) and traditional schoolbook multiplication (SBM). Hardware implementations of both proposed AThTKM multiplication archi-tectures are conducted on Virtex-7 FPGA Board using Xilinx ISE platform. The area-time-product (ATP) performance of the proposed AThTKM-I, based on ΔATP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, is better by 22.091%, 80.394%, 32.988%, and 5.277% than Direct Multiplication (DM), Traditional Schoolbook Multiplication (Traditional SBM), and CAThTKM, respectively, for 1024-bit inputs. Similarly, the performance of the proposed AThTKM-II, based on ΔATP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, is better by 17.751%, 79.302%, 29.254%, and -5.571% than Direct Multiplication (DM), Traditional SBM, and CAThTKM, respectively, for 1024-bit inputs. However, comparing both proposed methods of AThTKM (AThTKM-I and AThTKM-II), it can be inferred that AThTKM-II is 0.365%, 3.720%, and 5.277% better than AThTKM-I for 128 bits, 512 bits, and 1024 bits, respectively, while AThTKM-I is 1.080% better than AThTKM-II for 256 bits, respectively, thus demonstrating its area-time-product efficiency.

articleTitle: Low Power and High -Speed Sense Amplifier Design For 6T SRAM
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: A new model of a current sense amplifier has been proposed. This circuit is more efficient because of its better performance in operational parameters such as: power and time delay. Using a general model of static random-access memory consisting of six -transistors (6T), the proposed model of sense amplifier has displayed more efficient operation than the existing current sense amplifier models. Cadence Virtuoso software is employed for simulation experiments. In terms of power consumption, the proposed circuit performed 99.5% better than the traditional Alpha Latch-based sense amplifier and 1.08% betterthan the traditional current conveyor-based sense amplifier circuit. The proposed sense amplifier has overcome propagation delays of 83.38% and 99.99% respectively in the current conveyor and the Alpha Latch models.

articleTitle: Design of Arithmetic Logic Unit Using Energy Charge Recovery Adiabatic Logic Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In arithmetic logic units (ALUs), one-bit full adder cells are the most widely used digital circuit elements. Arithmetic operations are performed using Full-Adder (FA). They are also the core functionality of all computational circuits. Arithmetic and logic operations are performed by an arithmetic-logic unit, which is a component of a central processing unit. In this article, the objective is to lower the power consumption and increase design performance using adiabatic logic technique. For this, FA, Multiplxer, and ALU are designed using adiabatic logic are implemented and simulated in Mentor Graphics at 180nm technology. The results prove a total consumed power of 90.719 pW at supply of 1.8 V for FA and ALU has a total power consumption of 3.693nW and PDP 182.1*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−19</sup>.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Two-Dimensional Fractional-Order Riesz Digital Differentiator
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study examines the design considerations of the 2-dimensional fractional-order Riesz digital differentiator (FORDD). The initial task entails the creation of a 2-dimensional fractional-order digital differentiator (FODD) utilizing a 2-D discrete cosine transform (DCT). Then, it is demonstrated that the frequency response of the 2-dimensional fractional-order Riesz digital differentiator (FORDD) is only the scaling even part of the 2-dimensional conventional FODD frequency response. The design example demonstrates the use of 2-D DCT to assess the effectiveness of the suggested 2-dimensional fractional-order Riesz digital differentiator (FORDD). The outcomes of the simulation illustrate that the proposed 2-dimensional FORDD is more effective than the existing 2-dimensional fractional-order digital differentiator (FODD) which has 0.0395 of average magnitude error and 439.89 seconds of execution time.

articleTitle: Manifestation and Suppression of Nonlinearity Using Optical Phase Conjugation in Long Haul Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Optical phase conjugation (OPC) has been a prominent area of study in fields such as quantum electronics as well as nonlinear optics for the past thirty years. When two coherent optical beams travel in opposite directions with identical amplitude values and an opposite wave front, typically there is a unique relationship characterized between them by OPC. This report outlines the comprehensive design of an Optical communication model which suppresses nonlinearity via the use of Optical Phase Conjugation. The model is equipped with a CW laser having 32-input signals accompanied by extensive modules containing forks and Mach-Zehnder modulator. This design choice facilitates efficient and streamlined transmission of data through the communication model. Q-factor curves and eye diagrams are used to measure and extensively examine the proposed framework. The three stages of the model's design-light signal generation, nonlinearity addition, and optical phase conjugation with an optical loop mirror-all work together to improve output and overall performance.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection System and Techniques: Critical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: During the last few years, technological advancement has given significant improvement in drowsiness detection systems. The different experimental studies and data collected from these experiments have also improved the algorithms. This paper provides a detailed analysis of all these methods which have been developed till now. The paper also presents the drawbacks of these methods which will help in modifying the existing methods or developing new technologies. Furthermore, the paper represents the upcoming and recent challenges in drowsiness detection systems and discusses the practical and reliable approach. The paper presents a proposed solution that is more effective and economical.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning based Path Selection in Multi-hop Device to Device Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the computation time required to establish a multi-hop path between two devices using a reinforcement learning algorithm. The goal is to relieve the base station from traffic burdens and increase network efficiency. Path selection plays a crucial role in Device-to-Device (D2D) communication to reduce time delays in data transmission. Here, we attempt to establish a path by creating a multi-hop routing path. The device in the multi-hop path will act as a relay and establish D2D links with both the source and destination nodes. In this paper, the Dijkstra algorithm and reinforcement learning are used to find an optimum path for multi-hop communication. A hexagonal cell scenario is considered here by taking 25 numbers of cellular users, and the computation time for the number of communication requests is calculated using both algorithms. The reinforcement learning algorithm has a minimum computation time of 25 microseconds as compared to the Dijkstra algorithm. The computation time guarantees that the reinforcement learning algorithm minimizes time delay.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Decision Tree Classifier Performance in the Medical Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Accurate classification of diseases, such as heart disease and breast cancer, is crucial in the medical field. It enables early detection, appropriate treatment planning, and improved patient outcomes, emphasizing the need for precise classification models. This study aims to evaluate and compare the performance of three widely used decision tree classifiers, namely ID3, C4.5, and CART, using the Statlog heart disease dataset and the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Database (WBCD). Additionally, it explores the impact of oversampling, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning on the Machine Learning(ML) pipeline. Results indicate that C4.5 consistently outperforms ID3 and CART in both datasets. Furthermore, integrating oversampling, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning techniques with the C4.5 classifier notably improves F1 scores on the datasets. These findings underscore the significance of these components in enhancing classification efficiency, highlighting strategies for robust ML pipelines tailored to medical data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Accident Prevention with Alert Messages and Motion Sensors for Mountain Road Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The prevention of vehicle accidents in hilly places is a serious concern because of the particular difficulties presented by the topography and terrain. Drivers are faced with numerous challenges in hilly areas, such as steep grades, tight curves, small roads, and erratic weather, all of which raise the possibility of collisions. To reduce these dangers and improve road safety in hilly areas, this abstract examines several technologies and tactics. In this paper the prevention system that harnesses motion sensor technology to enhance road safety, particularly in challenging environments like remote or mountainous areas. The system detects sudden changes in vehicle motion indicative of potential accidents and promptly alerts nearby hospitals via real-time communication channels. By providing vital accident information to hospitals, such as location and severity, the system enables swift and well-prepared emergency responses. Through simulations and field tests, the efficacy of the system is validated, highlighting its potential to significantly reduce accident rates and mitigate the impact of road incidents. This innovative solution not only facilitates real-time accident detection but also streamlines emergency response efforts, ultimately improving overall road safety and saving lives. Moreover, the system's integration with existing intelligent transportation systems enhances its scalability and effectiveness. With its ability to expedite emergency medical assistance, this system represents a crucial advancement in accident prevention technology, promising to revolutionize road safety and emergency response protocols.

articleTitle: Minimizing Leakage Current & Ground Rail Fluctuations in 1-Bit 8t Full Adder Circuit Using Mtcmos Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Controlling leakage current and noise resistance has become crucial in the design of combinational and sequential circuits as technology moves closer to nanoscale scales. Multi-threshold CMOS is one extensively used method of addressing leakage current (MTCMOS). Nevertheless, even though the traditional MTCMOS method is good at lowering leakage current, it frequently causes variations in the ground rail while switching from low-leakage sleep mode to active mode, which affects the overall dependability of the circuit. In this case, by carefully sizing various transistors, a low-leakage eight-transistor (8T) based 1-bit complete adder is constructed. Optimisation algorithms are used to determine transistor sizes. In order to minimize leakage current even more, the improved 8 transistor full adder is subjected to a number of widely used leakage reduction approaches. Leakage current and ground fluctuation noise are compared using several widely used MTCMOS techniques. According to simulation studies, the improved 8T transistor can reduce sub-threshold current leakage by as much as 62% when used in conjunction with common MTCMOS methods.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of AIRBORNE SAR System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In today's modern era, SYNTHETIC APERTURE RADAR (SAR) is used extensively for military purposes, especially AIRBORNE SAR. Traditional AIRBORNE SAR system is comparatively complex, costly and are of large volume. It cannot be installed again and again for different applications, so we have developed an optimum AIRBORNE SAR system operating in X band which have all system parameter like azimuth resolution, antenna aperture length etc. in prime state. In this paper, SAR sensor designing is put into practice in order to satisfy a set of performance parameters. The modeling of design parameters for Spotlight and Stripmap mode of operations are stimulated. This paper illustrates how one single SAR system may function in both Spotlight and Stripmap modes and it also yields different resolution levels based on requirements at the expense of other factors.

articleTitle: Capacity Analysis of OTFS-Based Cooperative UAV Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The era of 6G is the generation of hyperconnectivity and ubiquitous networks. The next level of connectivity surpasses the benchmarks achieved using current 5G technologies. It indicates a pervasive network- everywhere and anytime for global coverage and to maintain connectivity in highly agile and unfavorable environments. To meet such specifications the latest modulation scheme- Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS), has arisen to be the pioneering technology for real-world scenarios for 6G. The next generation of communication requires connectivity in bullet trains, hyperloop transportation, racing cars, spacecraft, etc. OTFS delves into the realms of delay-doppler (DD) as an alternative to the arena of time-frequency (TF) employed for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM). OTFS leads to increased throughput as demonstrated by our simulation results. Cooperative communication further helps to enhance the link capacity.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of GaSb/InAs Heterojunction TFET for Gas Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In this study, a GaSb/InAs heterojunction TFET gas sensor is proposed to sense various gases. The motivation behind this work is improved sub-threshold slope and ON current resulting in better sensitivity by using a heterojunction TFET structure. Also, the multifaceted influence of oxide thickness on the energy band diagram and transfer characteristics of proposed device is investigated. The study systematically explores how varying the oxide thickness alters the energy band diagram and affects the transfer characteristics of the proposed gas sensor. Additionally, the research delves into the temperature variation of the proposed gas sensor, examining its impact on device performance. By analysing the interplay between oxide thickness, energy band diagram, and temperature, the study aims to impart comprehensive insights into the optimization and understanding of TFET-based gas sensor functionality.

articleTitle: A Deep Q-Learning based Architecture for 2 and 4 Users to Optimize Power Allocation and Signal Detection in NOMA Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Non-orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is a crucial technique in Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) that improves frequency band use efficiency. However, NOMA may encounter difficulties due to its complicated methods for canceling out interference and identifying channels, particularly when conditions change often. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel strategy that combines Power Allocation (PA) and Deep Learning (DL) to improve signal identification and interference manage-ment in NOMA systems with two or four users. We employ a Deep Neural Network (DNN) to detect signals and Deep Q-learning (DQL) to intelligently allocate power among users. This strategy improves our ability to recognize several users at once, as well as make decoding mixed signals easier and more efficient. Our technique performs far better in coping with the complicated and shifting situations seen in real-world communications. The findings reveal that Deep Q-Learning minimizes the complexity of interference cancellation and significantly improves the system's overall performance, addressing frequent concerns encountered in NOMA in CRNs.

articleTitle: Rice Plant Diseases Classification using a New Convolutional Neural Network based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In India, agriculture is a significant source of income and essential for livelihood. The majority of India's land is used to grow rice which is a fundamental component of diet. Plant diseases have a significant impact on rice harvesting which results in significant losses for the agricultural. Plant pathologists are trying to find a precise and trustworthy method to diagnose rice plant diseases. In past few years, machine learning techniques have been proven to be useful in the automated categorization of crop diseases. Presently, deep learning is widely used for disease detection in agriculture. In this paper, a new convolutional neural network (CNN)-based technique is developed to identify four different types of rice plant diseases: brown spot, bacterial blight, blast, and tungro. The proposed CNN architecture used in this study distinguishes diseases of rice plants based on deep features extracted from the five consecutive convolution layers with the activation function RELU. For experimentation of the proposed technique, a rice plant dataset of 5932 images are used. For the training of the CNN model, 4152 rice plant images are used while testing is performed using 890 images of four different classes. The classification technique used in this paper achieves 98.10% accuracy, 96.10% sensitivity, 98.72% specificity, 96.36% precision and 96.21% F1-score. The proposed technique offers better performance than many state of the art techniques.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study on Cyber Security and Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Cyber security is the defence against damage, intrusion, and unauthorized access to computer systems, networks, and data. It makes use of tools, procedures, and controls to protect data and prevent online attacks, guaranteeing the privacy, availability, and integrity of digital assets. In Today's world as technology increases rapidly the different types of cyber crime and cyber attacks also increases rapidly. Cyber attacks are threatening and purposeful effort to breach a computer system, network, or other device in order to hurt people, steal sensitive data, interfere with business operations, or get illegal access. There are several reasons for cyber attacks some of these are financial gain, industrial espionage, political motivation, personal vendetta, and cyber terrorism. In this paper, we study about different aspects of cyber security and cyber attacks. We also search about which type of attack is more dangerous in today's world research looked at various topics.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis and Review of Bandgap Reference Circuit for Wide Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Bandgap references are crucial components in numerous applications requiring stable and accurate voltage references. This comparative analysis delves into the performance evaluation of Bandgap Reference (BGR) circuit designed to operate effectively over a broad temperature spectrum. The study encompasses diverse BGR architectures, systematically accessing their performance, stability, and accuracy under varying temperature conditions. The primary objective is to identify the most suitable BGR circuit capable of delivering reliable performance across a wide temperature. Through meticulous comparison of critical parameters such as voltage stability, power efficiency, and temperature coefficient, this study offers valuable insights to guide the selection of an optimal BGR circuit tailored to the specific demands of varied temperature environments.

articleTitle: Compact Planar Antenna Loaded With H and S Slots for 5G and Advanced Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The study introduces the design and simulation of a novel slotted microstrip patch antenna specifically tailored for 5G wireless communication systems, utilizing the 2023 version of the High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software. The antenna operates at 24.47 GHz and 14.95 GHz and features a design that incorporates a ground plane, patch element, feed line, and source. The inclusion of slots in the patch enhances the antenna's performance. The ground measures 8 × 10 mm², while the patch has dimensions of 5 × 7 mm². The substrate is made from Rogers/RT Duroid-5870(tm), characterized by a dielectric constant of 2.2, improving the antenna's operational characteristics. The research focuses on assessing and enhancing key performance metrics of the antenna ensuring compatibility with the demands of 5G communication system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for LOS/NLOS Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Identification of Line of Sight (LOS) and Non Line of Sight (NLOS) is a challenging task since majority of physical effects that take place at distinct temporal/spatial conditions can affect the LOS propagation. Ultra Wide Band communication technology is the key technology in indoor positioning to identify LOS and NLOS communication channels in different environmental conditions. Different machine learning algorithms are used to identify on the basis of various training feature which basically exploits several static and time-varying features of the channel impulse response (CIR).In ML, the choice of training features plays a crucial role. The paper addresses machine learning techniques i.e. K-Nearest neighbour, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest in terms of their performance on different parameters.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna with Tilted Patch and DGS for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: A novel compact octagonal shape microstrip patch antenna with tilted patch is designed for radio frequency energy harvesting. A DGS technique in combination with tilted patch with respect to feed creates circular polarization at 6 GHz, 10.1 and 13.3 GHz having axial ratio bandwidth of 0.17 GHz, 1.88 GHz and 0.30 GHz respectively. The gain varies between 6.5 to 7.27 dB in the axial ratio bandwidth. The suggested antenna covers the entire frequency spectrum of UWB giving fractional impedance bandwidth of 141.7% (2.33 - 13.64 GHz). This compact, wideband and circularly polarized antenna can be utilized for ambient RF energy harvesting system. The results show that the antenna covers Wi-Fi and Bluetooth band (2.4 GHz, 5 GHz), WiMAX-band (3.5 GHz, 5.5 GHz), WLAN-band (5.2 GHz, 5.8 GHz) and X-band (8–12 GHz).

articleTitle: A NodeMCU-Based Programmable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a promising technology in metamaterial advancements for millimeter wave (mm-Wave) applications that could revolutionize future 6G wireless communications. RIS surfaces offers energy and spectrum efficiency by providing extended signal coverage and improved data rates. In this article, a compact RIS unit cell is realized, and its operation is demonstrated using simulation results. The footprint of the unit cell is 10x10x1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The unit cell is designed using an FR4 substrate with a G-shaped patch layer and full ground plane. The VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (Vanadium dioxide) is used as a reconfigurable element for getting beam-forming capability. The switching states give peak resonance at 24.3 GHz (OFF), 24.4 GHz, and 30.05 GHz (ON). The radiation efficiency at the operating frequencies is −13.75 dB, −7.63 dB, and −5.73 dB. The NodeMCU-based bias setup is demonstrated for getting the controllable states of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Hence, the programmable feature along with the beam forming capability is realized to meet the emerging trends and demands in mm-Wave 5G communications.

articleTitle: Blockchain Enabled Federated Learning-Based Medical Cyber-Physical System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques enlightened several areas and started a new era in industry. One challenging area is the Healthcare sector. The ML changed the direction and sped up the Healthcare sector and the Healthcare sector became Smart Healthcare (SH). The Medical Cyber-Physical System (MCPS) is effectively used in SH and it has several privacy and security issues. In such scenarios, Federated Learning (FL) has shown another direction to handle several challenges and opened an area for research. Additionally, blockchain (BC) technology has made the FL network secure. Inspired by several works in this paper Blockchain enabled FL- based MCPS is proposed that is capable of mitigating different adversarial attacks, Distributed Denial-of-Service, Sybil, etc. The performance of the FL is measured using accuracy, mean squared error (MSE), sensitivity, and specificity. After the final round achieved accuracy is 86%, MSE is 0.14, sensitivity is 89%, and sensitivity is 85%.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control of Distribution System FACTS Devices Using Deep Learning Models: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: FACTS device created for distribution system is entirely electronic. PI, PID, Series filter, and other controller components are popular for FACTS device design. This work aims to replace FACTS device controller components with deep learning models. To realize proposed FACTS devices, such as the DSTATCOM and DVR, input and output data from distribution system FACTS controllers are collected into a matrix or vector dataset. The developed deep learning-based FACTS device learns controller component behavior using these datasets. Since Deep Belief Nets (DBN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) learn differently, these models are used to evaluate their performance. The trained deep learning controllers replace the FACTS device in the IEEE 30 bus distribution system and are simulated for verification using PSAT and MATLAB Simulink. The goal is to detect similarities between the proposed and actual devices while putting the FACTS device optimally. The results demonstrated that DBN and CNN-based FACTS devices operate similarly to electronically-based ones. Therefore, deep learning-based DSTATCOM and DVR can intelligently operate the distribution system.

articleTitle: Arrhythmia Classification Using Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis is crucial for diagnosing and monitoring cardiovascular diseases. Accurate ECG signal classification is essential for early detection and intervention. This paper proposes a novel hybrid deep learning architecture for automated ECG signal classification using the widely known MIT-BIH Arrhythmia dataset. The architecture combines the strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for extracting spatial features from ECG waveforms and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks which will be used in capturing the temporal dependencies within the sequential data. This combined approach aims to achieve superior performance in ECG classification compared to models relying solely on CNNs or LSTMs. The CNN-LSTM model is trained as well as evaluated on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia dataset, achieving an accuracy of 98.94% surpassing several existing methods. This study contributes to the advancement of automated ECG analysis and offering potential improvements in cardiovascular disease diagnosis along with patient monitoring.

articleTitle: Wireless Interference Classification in Satellite Communications with the Standardized Variable Distances Learning Algorithm and Adaptive Spectral Domain Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Satellite communications has evolved significantly in recent years with the deployment of new communication satellites both in the traditional geostationary orbit (GSO) and non-GSO (NGSO) satellites. Wireless interference to satellite communication links either intentional (jamming) or unintentional (due to network engineering errors or equipment malfunction) can cause service degradation or denial of service. In parallel, machine learning and deep learning is increasingly used in the wireless communication domain and more specifically the satellite communication domain for a variety of tasks. On the other side, deep learning algorithm require significant computational resources and time for inference, which may be an issue for a fast detection and classification of wireless interferences. Then, this paper proposes the application of computing efficient distance-based machine learning (DML) algorithms to this problem. In particular, the Standardized Variable Distances (SVD) DML algorithm is used with an improvement based on the specific aspects of the wireless interference context. Instead of applying SVD directly to the original time domain representation of the satellite signal, this paper proposes a spectral domain approach where the characteristics of the wireless interference seen as outliers of the main communication signal are exploited to adaptively reduce the input data to the SVD algorithm for enhanced classification performance and robustness to noise. The concept is to use an outlier identification algorithm to identify the most discriminating segments in the spectral domain and then reassemble them as input to the SVD algorithm. The approach is applied to a recently published data set where three types of interference are generated for four different modulation schemes. The results show that the proposed approach is able to outperform other machine learning algorithms and the baseline where the entire spectral domain is used in input to the SVD algorithm

articleTitle: Efficient Chip Design of Penta Linear Array Charge Coupled Device (CCD)
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Charge coupled devices (CCDs) have historically played a crucial role in a variety of imaging and sensing tasks owing to their notable sensitivity, minimal noise, and impressive dynamic range. With technological progress, there is an increasing demand for CCDs with improved functionalities and efficiency to meet demands of various applications. One notable progression in CCD technology involves emergence of Penta Linear Array CCDs. This paper presents the design of a silicon-based CCD for space-based remote sensing in visible spectrum using Cadence Virtuoso software. The image sensor comprises linear five arrays, each linear array consisting of 6000 pixels. The pixel structure incorporates a 16×16 μm pinned photodiode, along with a storage gate, bias gate, transfer gate, and anti-blooming area. Each linear array is equipped with four readouts for charge-to-voltage conversion and amplification. The pixel array has been designed according to four poly and two metal layers. The clock fidelity simulations are performed using resistances and capacitances derived from the design layout in Cadence Virtuoso. The significant contributions of this paper lie in full chip CCD layout, encompassing subfield metal routing, device pad placement, and shield metal routing. The entire CCD chip design is thoroughly verified using design rule checks (DRCs), and subsequently generated a GDS file for fabrication.

articleTitle: Cooperative Deep Learning Strategy for Green Traffic Offloading in Heterogeneous Ultra Dense Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In the 6G era, energy efficiency and varying network traffic are a crucial concern because the power consumption of macro base stations (MBSs) is directly related to their traffic load and is comparatively high. In this regard, the emergence of ultra dense networks (UDNs) has revolutionized wireless communication by densely deploying small base stations (SBSs) to offload traffic from macro base stations (MBSs) while maintaining quality of service (QoS) for macro user equipments (MUEs). Nevertheless, traffic offloading causes network congestion, interference, and higher aggregate power consumption at the SBS, presenting significant challenges to the offloading process. This paper proposes a flexible traffic offloading scheme that utilizes system load information from both MBSs and SBSs to devise a green traffic offloading method, determine the optimal operational state for SBSs, and ensure the QoS for MUEs. In this direction, a multi-agent cooperative double deep Q-network is proposed, incorporating a policy learning technique based on value decomposition network to enhance long-term system performance. Numerical findings prove that the efficacy of the suggested method, in terms of energy efficiency and QoS for MUEs, is superior to existing methods.

articleTitle: Examination of the Total Defect Density and Thickness of CIGS Based PV cell through the SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The photovoltaic properties of CIGS/GaSe/ITO devices are investigated in this work with respect to the effect of active layer thickness and defect density. Important results with far-reaching consequences for solar cell technology have surfaced after a thorough investigation. These findings highlight the need for improvement of active layer thickness and meticulous control over defect density in order to improve device performance. The study clarifies the intricate relationships between active layer thickness, defect density, and important photovoltaic parameters as V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, FF, and PCE. Recombination losses and charge carrier collecting efficiency may be increased by reducing defect density, which in turn improves PCE, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, and FF. Similarly, one may improve light absorption while reducing negative consequences like increased series resistance and light absorption losses by regulating the thickness of the active layer. These results not only shed light on the basic principles that control the functioning of CIGS/GaSe/ITO devices, but they also provide workable ways to enhance their performance in practical settings. Scientists and engineers may use these findings to build solar systems that are more efficient and dependable, hastening the shift to renewable energy. In addition, there is great promise for future research in this area to develop renewable energy technology by fully realizing the potential of CIGS-based thin-film solar cells via the use of sophisticated production technologies and materials engineering tactics.

articleTitle: Developing a Temperature and Humidity Diagnostic System for the Optical and Electronic Infrastructure of a Primary Caesium Quantum Clock
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Caesium quantum clocks, pivotal in defining the SI second since the 13th General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1967, rely on intricate electronic and optical systems for precise timekeeping. Ensuring the accuracy of these systems requires monitoring and controlling environmental parameters like temperature and humidity, as fluctuations can lead to errors and potential damage. This paper presents the development of a diagnostic system using an Arduino UNO connected to a DHT11 sensor and ESP8266 Wi-Fi module to continuously monitor and transmit environmental data. The collected data is analyzed to maintain optimal operating conditions for the quantum clock infrastructure. Implementations using the IoT platform ThingSpeak demonstrate the system's capability for real-time data visualization and analysis. Statistical analysis of sampled data over a 30-minute interval shows a mean temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23.45^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and a mean humidity of 51.30%, with a strong correlation coefficient of 0.99 between the two parameters. A linear regression analysis further supports this relationship, indicating that for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> increase in temperature, humidity increases by approximately 5.11%. This diagnostic system not only ensures environmental stability but also aids in preventing inaccuracies in timekeeping, enhancing the reliability of caesium quantum clocks.

articleTitle: Steel Surface Defect Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis in steel sheets is an over-due technology in the steel manufacturing industry. Automated identification and categorization of defects will enhance product quality and improve manufacturing efficiency by limiting human error. Existing classifiers utilize supplementary feature extraction procedures to enhance accuracy and are equally effective as the procedure used. The preprocessing parameters are static, unable to adapt to respective defect types, leading to mediocre accuracy. As a result, the current inspection mechanism has scope for improvement. Therefore, this article introduces a deep convolutional neural network for detecting and categorizing damaged steel. The presented network utilizes 18 layers, framed like a VGG-16 architecture. The suggested approach attains an accuracy of 98.89%, which is better than existing methods. The results prove the framework's efficiency, paving the way for real-time examination of surface-level defects.

articleTitle: Water Body Detection Utilizing NDWI, NDVI and NMDWI Indices in SEN-12 Spectral Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the efficacy of water body detection utilizing three widely used spectral indices, namely Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), in SEN-12 spectral imagery. These indices are computed from the diverse spectral bands available in Sentinel-2 data to enhance our ability to identify and analyze water bodies. The SEN-12 dataset provides a rich source of multi-spectral information, enabling a nuanced exploration of these indices for water detection. Methodologies involve calculating and comparing NDWI, NDVI, and MNDWI across various scenes, assessing their strengths and limitations in different environmental contexts. The findings contribute valuable insights into the optimization of spectral indices for water body detection, thereby enhancing the utilization of remote sensing data for hydrological applications and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Dynamic Power Allocation with Energy Harvesting in Cooperative Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper delves into dynamic power allocation in Cooperative Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (CNOMA) network, emphasizing energy harvesting (EH). By integrating Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT), the study explores the impact of EH on system performance, achieving improved spectral efficiency and reduced energy consumption. This framework employs Time Switching (TS) and Power Splitting (PS) protocols, allowing for simultaneous EH and data transmission. Analytical derivations and simulations reveal that SWIPT-based CNOMA yields lower outage probability and increased achievable rates, especially for far users. This study also examines bit error rate (BER), outage probability, and achievable capacity across various channel conditions, demonstrating that cooperative communication and EH in Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks lead to significant performance gains. The results will contribute to the advancement of sustainable and efficient communication systems that can satisfy increasing needs for high data rates and reliable connectivity.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer

articleTitle: Detection of Bacteria on Food using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Due to their large global prevalence, foodborne illnesses have a significant negative impact on both the social economy and public health. Foodborne pathogens, the primary cause of foodborne illnesses, are crucial to the management and avoidance of foodborne illnesses. However, there is a limited percentage of true clinical pathogen detection in real life, and foodborne illnesses caused by many bacteria lack specificity in their clinical symptoms. Our objectives were to categorise foodborne illness pathogens using gas sensors and machine learning techniques, analyse foodborne disease case data, and choose relevant characteristics based on analysis findings in order to predict foodborne diseases.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Car Parking Detection Using YOLOv8 Deep Learning Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research paper introduces a novel approach for car parking slot detection using YOLOv8, an advanced object detection algorithm renowned for its state-of-the-art performance. The objective of this study is to address the increasing demand for efficient parking management in urban areas, where optimizing parking space utilization is essential to alleviate traffic congestion. The proposed model efficiently uses the power of YOLOv8's single-shot detection. It uses anchor boxes to automatically identify and classify vacant and occupied parking slots in real time. By utilizing YOLOv8's deep learning capabilities, the proposed method achieved impressive accuracy and efficiency in car parking slot detection. The simulation results showcase the system's effectiveness, providing valuable insights for urban mobility planning and management.

articleTitle: Exploring the Hidden Potential of Cyber Security Oriented Intelligent Data Hiding in Encrypted Images
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a surge of interest in the possibility of reversible data hiding inside encrypted images due to the promising practical uses of this technology, which include content owner identification, privacy protection, and encrypted picture authentication. Data hiding refers to the process of concealing data within a cover material. It is possible to conceal data in visual, auditory, textual, and graphical formats. Pictures, particularly digital pictures, can be used to conceal data. This data may be authentication details or author information, or it might be any text that is relevant to the image. The receiving end has to be able to decipher the encrypted data and restore the original picture. Advanced Cipher Logic based Data concealing (ACLDH) is a data concealing approach that meets this condition; it allows for accurate recovery of the host image. The losslessness of this method makes it well-suited for use in the medical field, the military, and cloud storage. After extracting the concealed data from an encrypted image, the suggested technique, known as ACLDH, may restore the original image to its original state without introducing any deformation. These days, reversible data hiding in encrypted graphics is all the rage because of its great quality: you can have your original cover back after removing the hidden data. It safeguards the initial data as well. Reversible Data Hiding (RDH) techniques that are now available for encrypted photos may be classified into two groups: those that do not preprocess the images and those that does. In this research, we show how to use adaptive thresholding to increase data concealing capacity and how to retrieve the original picture from a tagged image without distortion.
