articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Ge-Source Dielectrically Modulated TFET
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This study investigates a Germanium source dielectrically-modulated double gate TFET biosensor for identifying charged and uncharged biomolecules. Through dielectric modulation, biomolecules are immobilized in TFET nanogap cavities for label-free identification. Performance evaluation metrics including Drain current sensitivity, Sub-threshold Swing, Ion, Ion/Ioff, and Threshold voltage are employed. Silvaco TCAD simulations analyze the device's capabilities. The study demonstrates the potential of this biosensor for accurate biomolecule identification, offering a promising avenue for bioanalytical applications.

articleTitle: Attention-enabled Convolutional Autoencoder with Optimal Threshold to Detect Image Anomaly for Industrial Quality Assurance
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The process of automatically finding and localizing the available anomalies (or defects) in the images of the products is known as Image Anomaly Detection (IAD). In this paper, an attention-enabled convolutional autoencoder has been proposed to detect industrial defects using images of the products. The proposed model uses image-wise defect detection. The model classifies each test image as either defective or defect-free based on the magnitude of its reconstruction error. The Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) is employed to assess image quality by quantifying the reconstruction error. SSIM goes beyond comparing individual pixel values and analyzes the inter-relationships between local image regions. This incorporates luminance, contrast, and structural information, providing a more comprehensive evaluation aligned with human visual perception. Comparative result analysis and ablation study validate the superiority of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Real-Time Implementation of Spatial Audio on FPGA Using Interaural Time Difference and Amplitude-Driven Perceptual Depth
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper describes the real-time implementation of spatial audio effect using Basys-3 field programmable gate array (FPGA). The spatial audio effect in this paper is obtained by varying the azimuthal sound direction using interaural time difference (ITD) and amplitude-driven perceptual depth effect. In addition to the Basys-3 FPGA board, a peripheral module accessory (PMOD) I2S2 is used to take analog audio data from a mobile phone through an auxiliary-to-auxiliary cable and digitize it. This digitized data is then processed using a Verilog module and converted back to analog audio data using (PMOD) I2S2 to play the output audio through a pair of headphones. The introduction of varying azimuthal sound directions in the input data is carried out in real-time by introducing delays between the left and right audio channels of the data and a sense of perceptual depth is created by changing the amplitudes of the input data. A delay between the two channels is created by using a buffer. The amplitude of the input data is changed by scaling the input data. The delay between channels and the amplitude scaling varies dynamically with time. The effective deployment of techniques showcased in this paper promises FPGA-based approaches in audio processing for spatial audio. The findings offer important perspectives that can inform further enhancements of FPGA-based spatial audio rendering in audio processing.

articleTitle: Soldering Defect Identification Using Deep Learning and Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Electronic device functionality and dependability can be severely compromised by soldering flaws in printed circuit boards (PCBs). Effective quality control in manufacturing processes depends on automated flaw identification. Using a bespoke dataset of 500 photos of defective PCBs, this research proposes a novel approach for soldering defect recognition and summary creation on printed circuit boards (PCBs) using a combination of Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques. A framework for creating computer vision models is used to carefully classify these pictures according to six different defect categories: solder-bridge, solder-skip, overheated, offtrack-solder, overwetted, and underwetted. Total 300 images are classified into mentioned categories. To improve the model's performance and expand the dataset, the authors implemented augmentation methods, which led to the creation of a comprehensive 30% of total image dataset. The proposed system uses the Google Collab platform to train our unique dataset using the YOLOv5s model architecture, a deep learning model that helped us optimize the model to identify and categorize soldering faults properly. To ensure smooth implementation and reproducibility, we carefully recorded and downloaded the necessary dependencies for YOLOv5s. Preprocessing techniques for image enhancement were carried out on SVM algorithm to deploy the machine learning approach. To enable effective quality control measures in PCB manufacturing processes, our suggested methodology shows promising results in precisely identifying soldering faults.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Evaluaion of Solar Powered Electric Vehicle Charging Station Design Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: More than 1.3 million electric vehicles have been installed throughout the globe, and public charging networks for these vehicles are becoming increasingly common. It has been an area of interest to establish a plan for prioritizing the charging of electric vehicles (EVs) from a single network. This is particularly important in situations when the power source is restricted, such as with renewable energy, and for economic reasons (a higher price per KWh for quicker charging). When used in conjunction with electric vehicle (EV) charging, solar energy significantly decreases our reliance on fossil fuels. An electric car solar charger is created and constructed inside this system. In order to maximize the output from the solar panels, a dc-dc boost converter is used to transfer the voltage from the panels to the station's batteries. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is also included. Power the charging station with energy from the solar panels so that the vehicle's rechargeable battery may be charged. The charging station's status can be monitored at any time via the Internet of Things. We have created a solar-powered charging station to provide simple accessibility. Solar power is both a sustainable and accessible renewable energy source. Arduino controller for light-dependent resistor (LDR) light intensity monitoring, solar cell energy observation, battery charging, and cloud storage. The core idea behind the article is the IoT Solar Charging Station (IoTSCS), and it is tested by comparing it to the Classical Solar Charging Station (CSCS), a more traditional scheme, in order to see how well the new scheme works.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Stochastic Approximate Multipliers for Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In the age of edge computing, tiny and efficient neural network (NN) architectures are in high demand. Existing deterministic multipliers in neural networks suffer from high power consumption and space overheads. The research presents a novel Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementation of stochastic approximate multipliers (SAMs) to improve NN performance. SAMs are ideal for areas with limited resources, such as edge devices, since their components take up less space and consume less power. The technique utilizes SAMs' stochastic nature to lower power and space needs while preserving NN accuracy. The study includes detailed descriptions of the SAM architecture, hardware integration, training methodologies, FPGA implementation, and performance assessments. The proposed system, with inference rates of 8.6 ms and an accuracy of 97.5%, consumes 15.6 kWh of total energy, compared to the existing system's 22.1 kWh. The efficiency of the SAM-based FPGA NN architecture is demonstrated by decreased logic and memory usage, faster inference times, and improved accuracy retention. The results open up possibilities for the employment of energy-efficient, high-performance NNs in mobile and edge computing applications.

articleTitle: Disease Detection in Plant Leaves Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The paper proposes an automated approach for plant disease detection using transfer learning techniques. The study focuses on three critical agricultural crops-tea, potato, and tomato known for their economic significance and susceptibility to a range of diseases. Leveraging deep learning and transfer learning, the proposed system integrates pre-trained models such as VGG19, ResNet152V2, and InceptionV3, fine-tuned to classify plant leaf diseases with high accuracy. The dataset used in this study includes tea leaves with seven distinct diseases, potato leaves with three classes of diseases, and tomato leaves with ten disease classes. Pre-processing was done on these datasets to improve model training and guarantee homogeneity. This included resizing and data augmentation. The best-performing model for each crop was identified by analyzing the transfer learning models using a variety of measures, such as validation accuracy, confusion matrix analysis, and F1-score. By comparing various transfer learning models, this study demonstrates that deep learning-based approaches offer superior performance in plant disease detection. The improved accuracy and robustness of these models provide a more efficient solution for early disease identification, allowing for timely treatment and reduced crop losses. The ultimate goal of this paper is to support agricultural professionals and farmers in early disease detection, facilitating precision farming practices and contributing to increased agricultural productivity and sustainability. This technology has the potential to make a significant impact on food security and promote a more sustainable approach to agriculture.

articleTitle: Sugarcane Leaf Disease Classification Using Hybrid CNN and RNN
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Deep learning methods have shown promise in automating agricultural disease diagnosis. In this paper, a comparison of a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model and a hybrid Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model for identifying leaf diseases to determine which approach performs better in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The hybrid CNN, integrating EfficientNet and DenseNet, excels in image-based tasks, while the hybrid RNN, combining SimpleRNN and LSTM, is suited for sequential data processing. The objective is to assess these models based on performance metrics, computational complexity, generalization, and application suitability. Empirical testing shows the hybrid CNN achieved 94.8% accuracy and efficiency, outperforming the hybrid RNN's 36.4% accuracy and 4% efficiency. The results provide insights into each model's strengths and limitations, aiding decision-making for data analysis tasks. The choice between hybrid CNN and hybrid RNN models depends on data type and task requirements.

articleTitle: A Ladybug Beetle Coati Optimized Joint Energy and Spectral Efficiency Maximization in Cooperative Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Due to the rise in information rate prerequisite and the heterogeneity level, the alteration in network traffic in the upcoming wireless communication (WC) encompasses innovative challenges in the case of energy efficiency (EE) and spectrum management. Recently, multiple current frameworks have anticipated and expressed the cooperative spectrum sharing (CSS) technique in CR networks (CRN). Nevertheless, none of the frameworks provided effective solutions to maximize EE-SE performance and failed compatible with recent WC applications. Hence, the proposed framework introduces a novel hybridized metaheuristic-aided Ladybug Beetle Coati optimizer (LB-CO) technique for maximizing the EE-SE performance in the CRN system. The Python simulation tool is utilized for the experimentation process and various performance measures like EE by varying transmission power (TP) under different SNR conditions, and normalized SE by varying TP are examined and compared with other techniques. The overall EE of 14.78kb/J for 8dB SNR value and 80kHz BW and the normalized SE of 0.61bits/s/Hz is obtained by the suggested framework for enhancing the performance of the CRN system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Novel Technique's Performance in Terms of Energy Consumption, Security and Reliability using Simulations or Real-World Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are essential for many applications, such as industrial automation, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. As these networks continue to grow, ensuring the security and energy efficiency of data transmission becomes paramount. This research proposes a novel Secure Energy Consumption Technique (SECT) designed to address the simultaneous challenges of securing communication and optimizing energy consumption in WSNs. The SECT integrates advanced encryption algorithms and efficient key management protocols to fortify the security of data transmission within the network. By employing lightweight cryptographic techniques, the proposed solution aims to assault a balance between security and energy efficiency, ensuring that the overhead associated with encryption does not compromise the sensor nodes' restricted energy resources. Key features of the SECT include a dynamic key management system that adapts to the network's changing conditions, minimizing energy consumption while maintaining a robust security posture. Additionally, the technique incorporates energy-aware routing algorithms to optimize the path selection for data transmission, further reducing energy expenditure.

articleTitle: Enhancing Anatomical Landmark Detection in Brain Images through Multiagent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Identifying anatomical landmarks in medical imaging is critical for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. However, manual annotation varies widely among observers and demands specialized expertise. We propose an innovative approach using multi-agent reinforcement learning, based on the understanding that anatomical landmarks are interconnected and exhibit non-random configurations. Our framework employs a Deep Q-Network architecture with interconnected agents that collaborate by sharing knowledge during training, improving accuracy. It supports multiple agents, each tasked with identifying specific landmarks, and achieves a 50% reduction in detection errors compared to existing methods, while requiring fewer computational resources and less training time. This technology holds promise for advancing anatomical landmark recognition in brain imaging, facilitating more precise medical image interpretation.

articleTitle: Security Assessment of IoT Devices: A Contemporary Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: There has been a sudden spurt of the IoT devices like smart phones, smart watches etc owing to the progress in the field of telecommunications marked by introduction of 5G. These devices interact with the user in a more humane way which have led to their wide adoption all over the world providing different facilities like communication, entertainment, banking, e-commerce etc. The large scale usage of the devices has also led to adversaries targeting these devices leading to loss of data, money and life. This brings the requirement of the evaluation of the IoT devices from the security perspective. This paper gives a survey of the security analysis techniques of the IoT devices from all possible dimensions mainly focusing on the traffic analysis aspect. Recent papers from 2015 onwards have been surveyed which deal with various techniques and methodology for the traffic analysis of the IoT Devices. Finally, it is believed that this survey paper will add to the continuous investigation in the field of IoT device security analysis and generate interest in the present crop of researchers in this field.

articleTitle: Land Use Land Cover Classification Using Machine Learning and Remote Sensing Data: A Case Study of Karnaprayag, Uttarakhand, India
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) classification is crucial for planning and sustainable development, especially in mountainous regions. This study focuses on the Tehsil Karnaprayag, situated in the vicinity of the Greater Himalaya. With a total area of 1858.903 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and elevations ranging from 647m to 7641m. Using multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery and Machine Learning techniques i.e. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and K-nearest neighbor (KNN). This study aims to classify seven distinct land cover classes: snow, forest, water bodies, grassland, agricultural land, fallow land, and built-up areas. The classification results demonstrate the effectiveness of XGBoost classifier achieving an accuracy of 90.22% and a kappa value of 0.882, while KNN achieved an accuracy of 88.59% with a kappa value of 0.862. The analysis reveals that forest and fallow land are the predominant land cover types in the study area, constituting nearly 60% and 15% of the total area respectively. Notably, XGBoost exhibits the highest class-specific accuracy of 97.60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for the snow class, demonstrating its utility in discriminating between challenging land cover types. This research highlights the importance of LULC classification in informing land management strategies and facilitating sustainable development initiatives in mountainous regions. The findings provide valuable insights into the spatial distribution and composition of land cover in Tehsil Karnaprayag, essential for effective planning and conservation efforts in the Himalayan ecosystem.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of CNN-Based Speech Emotion Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), aiming to enhance human-computer interaction by enabling machines to recognize and respond to human emotions accurately. The study utilizes the Toronto Emotional Speech Set (TESS), a comprehensive dataset comprising approximately 2,800 utterances with diverse emotional states. The methodology involves pre-processing speech signals to extract Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, which are then converted into spectrograms and fed into a CNN model for emotion classification. The results demonstrate the model's robust performance in recognizing emotions such as anger, happiness, fear, and sadness with high precision and accuracy. The paper discusses the impact of various hyperparameters on model performance, highlighting the trade-offs between training time and accuracy. The findings underscore the potential of CNN-based approaches in SER, offering valuable insights for future research and applications in affective computing.

articleTitle: Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into Product Roadmap Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work focuses on AI and ML in product roadmap planning while also exploring solutions to the challenges of using feature-based roadmaps for strategic decision-making. Having covered the recurrent categories of roadmap and the roadmap-making process, they will proceed to the part where AI and ML are shown to save time, as well as help deliver more precise information on the potential target customers, as well as the current situation in the given market sector. They further discuss problems that could undermine the accuracy of outcomes, involving data quality and interpretability. The role of transparency, collaboration, and progress to tackle the problem is highly underscored. The best practices for engineering an AI-integrated product roadmap are drawn up which are namely setting the specific targets, developing solid data basis, promoting collaboration and which ought to be iterated respectively. Some actual examples will show how AI, including ML, opens a variety of fields and demonstrate how it can make business processes more innovative and better informed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cybersecurity: Development and Evaluation of a Secure Data Sharing Paradigm Based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: As time goes on and technology gets better, various data-sharing technologies are becoming more and more integrated into many different businesses. Therefore, data exchange and security are crucial for the data's value to be realized. Nevertheless, it is challenging to verify the authenticity of a basic data sharing method in order to detect electronic data usage traces. An further difficulty is the reluctance of data suppliers to provide their data. Employing Blockchain's distributed ledger, smart contract, data trust, and traceability features. For the purpose of facilitating secure access to data, this study introduces a blockchain-based data-sharing architecture that optimizes to circumvent the security and control issues associated with traditional centralized data sharing and administration. In addition, the research evaluates the practicality and safety of the prototype. Furthermore, this paper proposes a Secured Data Management Scheme (SDMS) that utilizes blockchain technology to optimize data sharing efficiency. To assess the efficacy of this model, it is cross-validated with the conventional Data Privacy Handler (DPH) method. While present centralized security solutions fail to meet security requirements in an IoT setting, blockchain technology provides a decentralized solution. Through the use of a blockchain and a WiFi-enabled network model, this article seeks to offer a secure communication framework for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. According to the results, attitudes and character quirks have a role in how the intelligence community plans to use a blockchain-based data-sharing model for integrating systems. This research demonstrated the viability of using blockchain technology in an intelligence community-centric data-sharing strategy.

articleTitle: Compression-Encryption Based Efficient Dual Image Watermarking for e-Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The requirement to protect the authenticity and accuracy of images motivates the implementation of water-marking on these images. Any alteration or interference with medical images might lead to erroneous diagnosis or treatment, as these images are vital for diagnosing and tracking diseases. Moreover, these photographs are regularly transmitted across the internet, increasing the potential for unauthorized access and alteration. Therefore, medical image watermarking is essential to safeguard the reliability and accuracy of these medical images in research and clinical environments. This paper presents a framework of a highly safe and reliable dual watermarking technique that utilizes the NSST-Radon transform to improve medical data security. The ultimate watermarked image is created by incorporating fingerprint and patient information into a medical image, resulting in dual watermarking. After embedding, the final watermarked image is compressed and encrypted to add a security layer. Moreover, our approach uses the best scaling factor to manage the robustness and imperceptibility tradeoffs. The experimental results indicate that the suggested approach demonstrates exceptional overall performance, a high level of imperceptibility, and resilience. The proposed scheme uses dual watermarking to safeguard original medical and non-medical images. The experimental and comparison results show that this strategy produces superior results with remarkable resilience, invisibility, and capacity.

articleTitle: Tech Harvest: Transforming Food Management with Intelligent Container Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The ultimate goal of innovation should be to develop a system that is stable and beneficial for society. The emerging revolution from the past decade of multiple low-cost sensors aims to develop multifaceted Internet of things (IoT) devices for uncountable industrial and home usage. The proposed sys- tem revolutionizes container regulation and quality assessment in mega kitchens, addressing various scenarios effectively. It employs ultrasonic sensors to detect container status, ensuring contents are fully covered. Gas sensors and load cells continuously monitor contents, sending data to a MySQL database via a PHP API. Ultrasonic sensor data, determined by container height, alerts users if lids are open, preventing spoilage from atmospheric gasses. Load cell data, amplified by the HX711 module, alerts users when contents fall below set thresholds, reducing manual checks and enabling timely supply orders. The Gas sensor in the container monitors various gases at different ppm levels and implements preventive measures to avoid Food spoilage. Updates occur every 2 seconds, ensuring real-time monitoring. This innovative approach significantly enhances food storage practices, minimizing wastage and mitigating storage issues. By providing timely notifications, alerts, and temperature monitoring, it empowers kitchen managers to optimize efficiency and economy, revolutionizing pantry management in high-volume kitchens. This Research work promises a more sustainable and efficient approach to food storage, embodying the potential of IoT technology to address critical challenges in the culinary industry.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Classifiers using Wav2Vec2.0 Layer Embeddings for Imbalanced Stuttering Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Stuttering is a speaking problem affecting normal fluency and flow of speech. Despite research done in this area, stuttering detection and identification is challenging in nature, due to the heterogeneity of audio samples which varies across people who stutter. This paper presents the application of extracting feature representations using pretrained deep learning models i.e. Wav2Vec2.0 (BASE & LARGE) and examines different data sampling methods for effective analysis. We have explored different sampling techniques i.e. oversampling and undersampling and evaluated their performance on traditional classifiers i.e. k-Nearest Neigh-bors (kNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naïve Bayes' Classifier (NBC), Random Forest (RF) where SVM performed the best. With this, we performed a comprehensive layer-wise analysis of Wav2Vec2.0 feature embeddings and observed that middle layers capture more stuttering information. Our results show significant improvements in unweighted average recall (UAR) using the KSoF [1] and Sep-28k [2] datasets. Specifically, we observed a relative increase of 15.5% & 24.4% in UAR for the KSoF and Sep-28k dataset, relative to the results reported in [3] and [4] respectively.

articleTitle: Development of a Sensor-Based Wearable Fetal and Maternal Health Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: According to the World Health Organization, approximately 360,000 pregnant women are registered annually in Sri Lanka. Among these, about 328,000 babies are born healthy, while 5,800 are born with birth defects, some of which are severe and impact daily life. To address the Sri Lankan stillbirth rate of 6.01%, continuous monitoring of fetal and maternal health is essential. Although commercial devices exist to fulfill this requirement, their high costs and safety issues often preclude regular use. To overcome these challenges, there is a need for a passive, wearable, and portable monitoring system for fetal and maternal health. This system should track key parameters such as fetal heart rate, fetal movements, and maternal heart rate to mitigate health risks for both the fetus and the mother. In this study, we developed a device using the Arduino, appropriate sensors, and a microcontroller to monitor these vital parameters. The device is user-friendly and suitable for regular use. MATLAB was utilized for the signal processing requirements of the proposed device. Test results demonstrated that fetal movement detection was accurate, although potential errors may arise during real-time testing. For pulse sensor readings, an average percentage difference of 3.025% was observed compared to pulse oximeter readings, likely due to placement errors and sensor instability in the proposed device.

articleTitle: Incremental Hybrid Decode-Amplify-Forward Source Retransmission Protocol for Outage Analysis of Relay-Assisted NOMA in PLC
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Power line communication (PLC) is a desirable technology that has gained prominence with the help of present wired infrastructure. With the ability to decrease interference and improve device propagation performance, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has been developed as a novel multiple access system. This study proposes a hybrid protocol performed in NOMA based PLC with relay assistance. The relay aided NOMA for PLC system models are initially created using a source, relay, and destination. The proposed hybrid relaying strategy using Incremental Hybrid Decode-Amplify-Forward Source Retransmission (IHDAF-SR) for NOMA system to improve signal transmission rage. Moreover, the power allocation of proposed method is minimize the outage probability by using Adaptive Honey Badger Optimization (AHBO) algorithm. The results of simulation demonstrate that the proposed method improves performance in terms of power allocation of outage probability (0.0094), average complexity (0.145) and spectrum efficiency (0.845).

articleTitle: Spectroscopy Sensor and Mobile App and Artificial Intelligence Integration for Real-Time Soil Analysis and Crop Management in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research proposes a major enhancement to a mobile application for agricultural recommendations by adding spectroscopic sensors for accurate detection of soil nutrients. The application, which is based on Firebase and Flutter, effortlessly integrates real-time data from color sensors (or spectroscopic sensors) to give farmers precise insights into the nutrient levels of their soil. The recommendation engine's integration of spectroscopic data requires quick deployment and effective management of real-time updates, which Firebase's server-less architecture provides. An improved recommendation engine powered by TensorFlow and Python and utilizing sensor and historical data is driven by the cross-platform Flutter framework, which offers an easy-to-use user interface. The app's ability to provide thorough soil nutrient assessments is enhanced by the color sensor integration, giving farmers more control over crop selection and nutrient management. Empirical evidence demonstrates enhanced agricultural yields and more efficient use of resources, highlighting the concrete advantages of this improvement. In order to further precision agriculture, this research explores the technical nuances of integrating spectroscopic data into pre-existing machine learning models. This study compares pre-existing machine learning algorithms to identify the most effective model for crop prediction using spectroscopic data. This study offers recommendations for future agrotechnological advancements by emphasizing the complementary roles of mobile applications and sensor technology in empowering farmers and enhancing agricultural sustainability.

articleTitle: Emphasis on Power Consumption Using Bluetooth LE and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Wireless communication has become a transformative impact on numerous sectors, leading to the creation of novel products and functionalities. Among these technologies, Bluetooth Low Energy has emerged as an important protocol first introduced in 2009 to meet needs of low power and battery-operated devices. With years passing by, Bluetooth LE went through substantial changes including low duty cycle directed advertising, secure connections with data length extension, and new PHY layer types enhancing throughput. These improvements have established the position of Bluetooth LE as a foundation for both consumer electronic and engineering industries. The objective of this paper is to discuss intricacies that characterize Bluetooth LE by focusing on its diverse features that influence device performance. By assessing these parameters, the study intends to provide suggestions towards maximizing Bluetooth LE utilization for different applications. Further, it looks at possible uses of features in Bluetooth LE in this paper. Consequently, aiming to contribute an improved understanding about what can be done using Bluetooth Low Energy as well as its potential role in wireless communications innovation in future years.

articleTitle: Safe Route - IoT and AI-based Fire Evacuation System for Smart Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative approach using IoT sensors and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to optimize evacuation routes in emergency preparedness. The system architecture allows for seamless communication between IoT sensors and the ACO algorithm, enabling timely decision-making in emergency scenarios. The study uses diverse datasets to enhance adaptability and comprehensiveness, paving the way for a transformative paradigm in fire safety for smart buildings. The ACO algorithm's performance is compared with Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm. Evaluation criteria include convergence time, number of iterations, and total running time. Results show that the ACO algorithm consistently outperforms or matches other algorithms across all graph complexities. It converges faster and achieves shorter runtimes, with improvements becoming more pronounced as graph complexity increases. The ACO algorithm's effectiveness in solving complex shortest path problems is demonstrated through rigorous analysis and comparison.

articleTitle: FPGA-Optimized Seven-Term Karatsuba Multipliers for Large Integer Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Efficient multiplication of large integer polynomials is essential in modern cryptographic systems. This research delves into the seven-term Karatsuba multiplication method, renowned for its efficiency but often overlooked due to its intricate sub-multiplications. The study concentrates on implementing both asymmetrical and symmetrical versions of seven-term Karatsuba Multiplication (ASeTKM-I, ASeTKM-II, SSeTKM-I, and SSeTKM-II) to enhance speed and hardware utilization. To assess performance, the Area-Time-Product (ATP) metric is computed and compared against conventional asymmetrical and symmetrical seven-term Karatsuba multiplication techniques (CASeTKM and CSSeTKM), as well as contemporary methodologies. Hardware implementations on Virtex-7 FPGA device in Xilinx ISE platform reveal that the most effective proposed method (ASeTKM-I) surpasses other designs. It exhibits superiority, being 19.443%, 79.728%, 39.632%, 5.346%, 37.796%, 6.720%, and 2.616% better than Direct Multiplication (DM), Traditional Schoolbook Multiplication (Traditional SBM), CASeKTM, PASeKTM-II, CSSeTKM, PSSeTKM-I, and PSSeTKM-II, respectively, for 1024-bit inputs.

articleTitle: Nano Functionalized Antenna Based IoT Enabled Devices for Health Care Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is crucial in diabetes management, necessitating the development of advanced sensing technologies. This study proposes a novel approach utilizing nano functionalized antenna-based IoT-enabled devices for CGM applications. The proposed method harnesses the unique properties of graphene, including high electrical conductivity, large surface area, and biocompatibility, to enhance glucose sensing capabilities. Evaluation of graphene-based materials involves assessing their electrical conductivity, surface area, and biocompatibility using techniques such as four-point probe measurements, BET analysis, and biocompatibility assays. A comparison with existing CGM models highlights the advantages of the proposed method, including high sensitivity, biocompatibility, miniaturization, and integration with IoT platforms. Numerical ratings on various parameters provide a quantitative assessment of the proposed method's performance relative to existing models. Overall, the proposed nano functionalized antenna-based IoT-enabled devices offer a promising solution for accurate and reliable CGM, with potential implications for improving diabetes management and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Reversible Arithmetic Logic Units (R-ALU) Using Verilog
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Optimizing power consumption in circuits can be facilitated by exploring reversible computing within Quantum QCA design alongside CMOS architecture design. This paper introduces a comparative examination of four Reversible Arithmetic Logic Units. Certain parameters such as number of Reversible gates utilized, Dynamic & Static power, Area (Slice Look up tables consumed/LUT), Input-Output blocks (IOB), Garbage bits, No. of Arithmetic and Logical Operations performed have been studied. Among the examined reversible arithmetic logic units, ALU-D1 stands out for its minimal dynamic and static power consumption, totaling a typical process power of 2.769 watts. Following closely is ALU_RM, with a typical process power of 3.097 watts. ALU-D1 and ALUD2 exhibit the lowest IOB count, specifically 12, and also have the least Slice LUT consumption at 4/14400. In terms of construction, ALU-D1 and ALU-D2 utilize 11 reversible gates, while ALU_RM and ALU_RUG employ 14 and 13 reversible gates, respectively. Both ALU-D1 and ALU-D2 excel in executing 18 operations each, whereas ALU_RM and ALU_RUG handle 16 operations each. In nearly all aspects, ALU-D1 and ALU-D2 outperform their counterparts, except for a higher consumption of garbage bits in their construction. The study involves the implementation of various reversible Arithmetic Logic units using Verilog in Vivado ML Edition – 2023.2 for FPGA, targeting the Zynq-7000 family of FPGAs.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Experimentation on Security-Conserving Storage Verifications and Data Dynamics Over Cloud Storage Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: As an IT firm moves into the future, cloud computing is quickly becoming the standard. The data centre serves as a centralized server from which data may be accessed. Businesses are quickly moving their operations to the cloud in order to take use of the most efficient resources. Both data dynamic operation and public verifiability at a single instance are supported by the current technologies. Instead of involving the client in auditing to detect cloud-stored data, the suggested approach takes into account the duty of a third-party auditor to guarantee the data's integrity. Data operations for inserting, deleting, and modifying data on the block are provided by data dynamics. A novel cloud data enrichment technique dubbed Advanced Cipher based Data Dynamics and Storage Model (ACDDSM) is presented to avoid the flaws in the previous system. To clearly assess the suggested model's performance, it is cross-validated with the traditional Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman (RSA) method. One possible solution to this issue is a cloud server. Managing storage on a grand scale is within its capabilities. But since it is a third-party service, data security is a concern. Strong encryption methods can be used to safeguard data from the cloud server. We must first distinguish between sensitive and non-sensitive data in order to implement appropriate data security measures. Prioritizing sensitive data above potential dangers is essential. Finding valuable information within a reasonable amount of time to compute is the main topic of this research.

articleTitle: Built-Up and Land Use Land Cover Mapping for Sustainable Planning in Himalayan Region by Using Machine Learning and Sentinel-2 Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The Himalaya region, known for its ecological sensitivity, also faces recurring natural hazards such as earthquakes, landslides, sinking, glacier bursts, and flash floods, which necessitate the implementation of effective planning and management strategies to ensure sustainable development. This study focuses on Joshimath, a subdivision of Chamoli district in Uttarakhand, India, situated in the Greater Himalaya region, covering an area of 4563.52 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Our objective is to map built-up areas using Machine learning techniques and Sentinel-2 satellite multispectral imagery to support sustainable planning initiatives. Two machine learning models, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were employed in this study. RF achieved an overall accuracy of 92.62% with a kappa value of 0.911, while SVM achieved an accuracy of 90.557 with a kappa value of 0.886. Precision and recall metrics for the built-up class were calculated, with RF achieving 94% precision and 83.22% recall, and SVM achieving 93.48% precision and 82.24% recall. Additionally, the total area classified as built-up by RF was 236.96 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, whereas SVM classified 198.67 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of machine learning techniques, particularly RF and SVM, in accurately mapping built-up areas in the Himalaya region. This information is crucial for sustainable planning and management practices, enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions regarding land use and development while preserving the ecological integrity of the region.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Mixed FSO/RF based HAPS Relaying Communication Network using MP-PPM Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Information and communication technology have significantly increased and advanced in recent years. But the ever-inflating data and numerous media services requirements has resulted in congestion in the conventionally used RF spectrum, necessitating a move from radio frequency (RF) carriers to optical carriers. Free Space Optical (FSO) communication systems are becoming a feasible choice for many applications due to their low power consumption, wide bandwidth broadband availability, and low implementation costs. This paper examines a mixed FSO/RF-based HAPS-assisted communication network, in which HAPS works as a decode & forward relay. Since FSO follows line of sight (LOS) communication, the Source Ground Station (SGS) to HAPS link is presumed to be an FSO link. Consequently, the HAPS to Destination Ground Station (DGS) link is regarded as a nakagami-m distributed RF link, allowing it to serve many ground destinations. Operating at a height of 20 kilometers in the stratosphere, a High Altitude Platform Station (HAPS) can significantly advance the concept of a 6G network. However, since the HAPS is quasi-stationary, the FSO link connecting SGS to HAPS suffers from atmospheric turbulences and pointing error losses. In this paper, MP-PPM modulation is taken into account which enhances the performance of the FSO link compared to the conventional On-off keying (OOK) modulation and the results of both are compared. The performance is evaluated by obtaining the expressions of outage probability and Error rate by considering all the situations stated above.

articleTitle: Digital Cropping: A Comparative Analysis of Hybrid CNN-XGBoost With Stacking & Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Prediction of crop yield is crucial for farmers and governments worldwide to maximize profit and make informed decisions. Earlier investigations employed statistical methods but nowadays, Artificial Intelligence-based algorithms have emerged as practical tools for predicting the yield of crops. In this direction, the present study evaluates the effectiveness of various machine learning and deep Learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GBR), Bi-LSTM, LSTM, XGBoost, CNN-XGBoost, Stacking, Averaging, Bagging, and Linear Regression, in forecasting crop yield. The study was conducted on a dataset consisting of crop information about Rabi and Kharif season attributes with meteorological factors from 1997 to 2015 for different states in India. The models were compared and evaluated using various evaluation metrics. Our results showed that the Gradient Boosting method and stacking of machine learning techniques outperformed the existing baseline approaches with 98% prediction accuracy. Machine learning methods produced promising results in comparison to the regression model. By offering valuable insights into utilizing machine learning algorithms, our study contributes to crop yield prediction for diverse crops. The findings can assist farmers and stakeholders in making informed decisions about enhanced crop management practices.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches and Security Domains in Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Sentiment recognition from voice signal is an important but challenging element of human machine interaction. In the state of art many machine learning techniques have been utilized to recognize the emotions from text sources available in social media. Recently, deep learning techniques has become an alternative to recognize emotions from speech signal. This paper explores the power of deep learning techniques, highlighting their success across diverse fields like e-commerce, business planning, mental health evaluation, image and speech recognition, natural language processing, and more. It provides a comprehensive review of popular deep learning methods, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Deep Belief Networks (DBNs). Additionally, the paper compares and contrasts traditional machine learning approaches with deep learning methods. Different security domains and issues in social media w.r.t social media users, their information are covered in this paper.

articleTitle: A Literature Review on the Advancements in Hybrid Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper surveys the recent advancements in the area of perovskite solar cell (PSC) technology. Recent studies are discussed, covering novel materials, device architectures, and fabrication techniques aimed at enhancing PSC efficiency, stability, and scalability. Key findings of this paper include the superior performance of dual-layer mesoporous designs, such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TiO_{2}+Al2O_{3}$</tex> configurations, which minimize current leakage and optimize electron insulation. Additionally, research on ionic-to-electronic current amplification in hybrid PSCs demonstrates a new pathway to improve solar energy conversion. Other studies focus on optimizing electron transport layers (ETLs) and hole transport layers (HTLs) to enhance device performance and stability. Innovations in inverted PSCs, novel hole transporting materials (HTMs) like DEG-IDIDF, and the development of 2D3D hybrid perovskites further contribute to improving PSC efficiency and durability. These advancements hold promise for the development of cost-effective, efficient, and stable solar energy solutions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Accessory for Self Defense
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: In an instance when fears about personal safety are growing, especially for the weaker members of society like the physically impaired, inventive technological solutions are essential. This study describes a multifunctional self-defense gear that combines cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to lessen potential threats. The add-on uses a pulse sensor to recognize high heart rates that could be a sign of danger. This allows a camera to be activated in order to analyze the threat. The ML algorithms use facial gesture analysis and prerecorded photographs of known criminals to evaluate the scenario and, if needed, trigger a small pepper spray module for immediate defense. The gadget also has a GPS tracker built in to notify local authorities of the user's location in the happening of an emergency. The captured video is securely kept on a cloud-based stand that is only accessible to the owner, escalating the usefulness of the add-on as a prophylactic and possible proof lest of an urgent situation. This essay describes the self-defense accessory's development, application, and assessment, emphasizing how it might deeply improve private security for people of all ability levels.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Speech Enhancement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Noise presents a significant challenge in signal processing, especially with speech signals that are prone to various types of acoustical disturbances like babble noise or street noise. The ability to predict and remove noise effectively depends on how rapidly the noise changes relative to the speech. Filtering techniques have been developed to address these challenges and improve speech quality. This paper examines and contrasts three prevalent filtering techniques: The Wiener filter, Kalman filter, and Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm. It assesses their performance based on various metrics including spectrogram quality, Mean Squared Error (MSE), computation time and Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) scores. By conducting simulations with varied noisy speech signals across different noise environments, the research assesses the effectiveness of each approach concerning spectral accuracy, noise attenuation capability, perceived speech quality, and computational efficiency. This evaluation seeks to assist in identifying appropriate speech enhancement methods tailored to particular application requirements and noise profiles.

articleTitle: EEG Graph-Based Disease Analysis: A Novel Approach to Neurological Disorder Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: EEG use in clinical neurophysiology is a keystone for diagnosing neurological disorders. This paper highlights studies that have been done on the application of machine learning to diagnose three common neurological conditions through EEG signals; epilepsy, stroke and migraine. We looked at different researches to determine the specificity of EEG signals in these diseases and the efficiency of various techniques. The results show that machine learning models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) greatly increase diagnostic accuracy. CNN had the best performance metrics among all models for both migraine and stroke diagnoses while SVM was superior in detection of epilepsy. When multiple diagnostic markers from EEG signals are combined, sensitivity and specificity improve for these neurological conditions detection. This comprehensive review underscores the potential of EEG-based machine learning techniques as a supplementary method for accurate diagnosis and monitoring of migraine, epilepsy, and stroke, providing a robust framework for future research and clinical practice. articleTitle: GAN-Based Image Augmentation and Comparative Analysis of Various CNN Models for Monkeypox Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: The outbreak of monkeypox across 75 nations has made this epidemic a major threat to the public health. Monkeypox similarity in clinical features to those of smallpox, chickenpox and measles makes it difficult to identify. Effective management and treatment of monkeypox relies on early diagnosis as well as identification. Previous researches have evaluated various deep learning approaches; however, they were conducted on a small dataset available in public domain, which impacts the learning of deep learning models and eventually impacts their precise accuracy and error rates. The goal of this study was to identify and verify the most effective methodology for monkeypox detection by comparing various deep learning techniques and classification models with significantly large dataset. For this reason, a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) was used in this study to generate 4142 augmented images from 414 images present in original dataset available in public domain which increased the dataset size 10 times with respect to the original dataset. Six popular deep learning models (EfficientNetB3, VGG19, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, VGG16 and InceptionV3) were developed and trained using generated large dataset and evaluated on different parameters to find the best performing one. The results of our experiments show that the EfficientNetB3 model performed the best in terms of classification with an accuracy level of 98.46% whereas other models like VGG16, VGG19, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2 and ResNet50 respectively resulted in 96.76%, 93.78%, 85.68%, 75.25%, 69.01% accuracies. Our findings demonstrate that for classification of images for monkeypox, the EfficientNetB3 approach performs better than other models. In the terms of both test and training sets also, it demonstrated a great level of precision in categorizing monkeypox images, hence it can be a useful asset for prompt and precise diagnosis in clinical situations. These findings seem promising since they highlight how deep learning techniques can be employed for early detection of monkeypox.

articleTitle: Implementation and Experimental Analysis of Anti-Theft Alarm System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This work, Anti-Theft Alarm System using Arduino and Force Sensor offers a practical and accessible solution to the pervasive issue of theft. Utilizing readily available components like Arduino microcontrollers and force sensors makes anti-theft technology more accessible to a broader audience. The system's affordability and ease of installation make it an attractive option for homeowners, vehicle owners, business proprietors, and anyone else looking to protect their valuables. The incorporation of an Arduino microcontroller adds a significant degree of flexibility and adaptability to the system, allowing it to be customised to meet the specific needs of individual users. This versatility ensures that the system can be tailored to suit various environments and scenarios, enhancing its effectiveness in preventing theft. Furthermore, the system's ability to sound an alarm and send short message service (SMS) notifications to the owner's phone when a pre-set force threshold is exceeded enhances its utility. It ensures prompt action in the event of a potential theft attempt. By providing owners with timely alerts, the system enables them to take immediate steps to protect their possessions and prevent theft. Overall, the anti-theft alarm system using an Arduino and force sensor represents a valuable contribution to the security sector. Its simplicity, affordability, and efficacy make it an appealing option for individuals seeking to safeguard their valuable belongings from theft or burglary.
